phrases.source: Legend of the Galactic Heroes (JP Eng) (Media Added)

phrases.japanese: 一度聞いたことがある
phrases.reading: いちど きいた こと が ある
phrases.lemmaField: 一度 聞く こと が ある
phrases.translation: Once heard-thing is there -> I heard about this once.
phrases.notes: ichido: once; one time; on one occasion

phrases.japanese: そっちの２人は見たことがあるな
phrases.reading: そっち の ふたり は みた こと が ある な
phrases.lemmaField: そっち の ２人 は 見る こと が ある な
phrases.romaji: socchi no futari ha mita koto ga aru na
phrases.translation: As for those two over there (close to the listener), [I] saw-matter exists -> I've already seen these two over there.
phrases.notes: futari: two persons, two people, couple

phrases.japanese: 味わったことがあるのか
phrases.reading: あじわった こと が ある の か
phrases.lemmaField: 味わう こと が ある の か
phrases.romaji: ajiwatta koto ga aru no ka
phrases.translation: Tasted-thing exists? -> Have you tasted this (food) before?
phrases.notes:
ajiwau: to taste; to savor

I hope you get the pattern by now, some more "koto" sentences follow and then we'll continue with compound sentences.

phrases.japanese: その目は見たことがある
phrases.reading: その め は みた こと が ある
phrases.lemmaField: その 目 は 見る こと が ある
phrases.romaji: sono me ha mita koto ga aru
phrases.translation: As for those eyes, I've already seen them.
phrases.notes: me: eye, eyes

phrases.japanese: 一度だけ見たことがある
phrases.reading: いちど だけ みた こと が ある
phrases.lemmaField: 一度 だけ 見る こと が ある
phrases.romaji: ichido dake mita koto ga aru
phrases.translation: Saw only once-thing is there -> I've seen this only once.
phrases.notes:
dake: only

I think Tae Kim covers "dake" in more detail later, but this sentence fits in here well.

phrases.japanese: 綾野さんのおばあさんの
phrases.reading: あやの さん の おばあさん の
phrases.lemmaField: 綾野 さん の おばあさん の
phrases.translation: [This item] is ayano's grandmother's?
phrases.notes:
obaasan: grandmother

Remark: The trailing "no" here is not the explanatory one, this is something I forgot to explain. If the explanatory "no" follows a noun or a na-adjective, there's a "na" added in between to distinguish it from the "no" used for linking a property. Don't worry about this for now, more examples are added soon. Tae Kim explains this here.

phrases.japanese: おばあちゃんから聞いたことがあるの
phrases.reading: おばあちゃん から きいた こと が ある の
phrases.lemmaField: おばあちゃん から 聞く こと が ある の
phrases.romaji: obaachan kara kiita koto ga aru no
phrases.translation: [I] heard [this] from grandma-matter exists -> I heard this from grandma (in an explanatory tone).
phrases.notes: obaachan: cute / familiar way to refer to a grandmother

phrases.reading: あるばいと
phrases.lemmaField: アルバイト
phrases.translation: arubaito: part time job
phrases.notes: This word is derived from the German word "Arbeit", which means "work, job". While this refers to a full-time job in German, it's just a part time job in Japanese. Japanese people are known to work hard, after all ;).

phrases.reading: ばいと
phrases.lemmaField: バイト
phrases.translation: baito: short for arubaito (part time job)
phrases.notes: This abbreviation is more common.

phrases.reading: きょう も ばいと
phrases.lemmaField: 今日 も バイト
phrases.translation: Work today, too? -> You're also working today (part time)?
phrases.source: Higurashi no Naku Koro ni S1 (JP Eng)

phrases.reading: おふろ に も いません
phrases.lemmaField: お風呂 に も いる
phrases.translation: [He] is not in the bathroom either.
phrases.notes: ofuro: bath, room where people take a bath

phrases.japanese: 私とごはんを食べませんか
phrases.reading: わたし と ごはん を たべません か
phrases.lemmaField: 私 と ごはん を 食べる か
phrases.romaji: watashi to gohan wo tabemasen ka
phrases.translation: Don't you want to eat with me?

phrases.japanese: とても強いので注意を
phrases.reading: とても つよい ので ちゅうい を
phrases.lemmaField: とても 強い ので 注意 を
phrases.translation: Because [it / someone] is very strong, be careful.
phrases.notes:
chuui: caution; being careful; attention

"node/ので" can be used to indicate a reason in the same way as "kara/から": reason node result -> because of "reason", "result" happened.

There are subtile difference between "kara" and "node": First, "kara" is more casual than "node". Second, ので puts emphasis on the reason, whereas から puts emphasis on the result. For casual listening comprehension, it's totally fine to just ignore this - have a look at the references if you want to know more.

phrases.reading: なまえ を つけた か
phrases.lemmaField: 名前 を 付ける か
phrases.translation: Did you attach a name [to someone] -> did you already name it? E.g. your new pet.
phrases.notes:
tsukeru: to attach
namae wo tsukeru: to name

"tsukeru" has a lot of different meanings, just have a look at the dictionary. It is used in many different contexts, which confused me in the beginning.

phrases.japanese: 名前は俺が付けました
phrases.reading: なまえ は おれ が つけました
phrases.lemmaField: 名前 は 俺 が 付ける
phrases.translation: As for name, I attached it -> I named [something].
phrases.notes:
tsukeru: to attach
namae wo tsukeru: to name

phrases.japanese: 名前がなかったので私がつけた
phrases.reading: なまえ が なかった ので わたし が つけた
phrases.lemmaField: 名前 が ない ので 私 が つける
phrases.romaji: namae ga nakatta node watashi ga tsuketa
phrases.translation: Because there was no name, I attached one -> Because something didn't have a name, I named it.
phrases.notes:
"node/ので" can be used to indicate a reason in the same way as "kara/から": reason node result -> because of "reason", "result" happened.

There are subtile difference between "kara" and "node": First, "kara" is more casual than "node". Second, ので puts emphasis on the reason, whereas から puts emphasis on the result. For casual listening comprehension, it's totally fine to just ignore this - have a look at the references if you want to know more.

phrases.reading: すぐ に わすれる ので
phrases.lemmaField: すぐ に 忘れる ので
phrases.translation: [I write it down] because I soon will forget.
phrases.notes: Just as for "kara", the result of something may be omitted for "node", if it is clear from context:

phrases.japanese: 私はかまいませんので
phrases.reading: わたし は かまいません ので
phrases.lemmaField: 私 は かまう ので
phrases.translation: [Don't worry] because I don't mind.
phrases.notes: Just as for "kara", the result of something may be omitted for "node", if it is clear from context:

phrases.reading: き を つける みんな
phrases.lemmaField: 気 を つける みんな
phrases.translation: Attach you mind, everybody -> The Japanese way to say: Be careful!
phrases.notes: ki: spirit; mind; heart​
phrases.source: Boku no Hero Academia_ Futari no Hero

phrases.reading: なぜ うそ を つく
phrases.lemmaField: なぜ 嘘 を つく
phrases.translation: Why do you lie?
phrases.notes:
uso: lie, sometimes also joke (noun); this is often used together with "tsuku":
uso wo tsuku: to tell a lie

phrases.reading: うそ つかない
phrases.lemmaField: 嘘 つく
phrases.translation: [You're] not lying?

phrases.japanese: お父さんまた嘘つきました
phrases.reading: おとうさん また うそ つきました
phrases.lemmaField: お父さん また 嘘 つく
phrases.translation: Father lied again.

phrases.reading: うそつき
phrases.lemmaField: 嘘つき
phrases.translation: usotsuki: liar

phrases.japanese: 何でよおかしいよおかしいよこの家
phrases.reading: なんで よ おかしい よ おかしい よ この いえ
phrases.lemmaField: 何で よ おかしい よ おかしい よ この 家
phrases.romaji: nande yo okashii yo okashii yo kono ie
phrases.translation: Why? [You are] weird! [This] family is weird!
phrases.notes: "ie" in this case refers to the entire family or everybody living in this house. The speaker was just slapped by her mother for saying something she thought was reasonable, so she said this. The official translation is: 'What was that for? You're crazy, you know? Everybody in this house is out of their mind!'

phrases.japanese: すみません遅くなりました
phrases.reading: すみません おそく なりました
phrases.lemmaField: すみません 遅い なる
phrases.translation: Excuse me, [it] became late -> I'm late.

phrases.reading: どう する つもり な の
phrases.lemmaField: どう する つもり だ の なの
phrases.translation: How do-intention it is? -> How do you want to do this? Or also: What do you want to do now?
phrases.notes: If "no" is used in the explanatory role after a noun or na-adjective, there's usually a "na" in front of it. I forgot to explain this, Tae Kim explains the reason on p. 67 or here. Without the "na", it sounds like you'd link the noun to another thing clear from context.

phrases.reading: わたし は だれ な の
phrases.lemmaField: 私 は 誰 だ の
phrases.translation: As for me, who am I (asking for explanation, maybe he lost his memory).
phrases.notes: If "no" is used in the explanatory role after a noun or na-adjective, there's usually a "na" in front of it. I forgot to explain this, Tae Kim explains the reason on p. 67 or here. Without the "na", it sounds like you'd link the noun to another thing clear from context.

phrases.reading: あなた が すき な の
phrases.lemmaField: あなた が 好き だ の
phrases.translation: [He] likes you?!
phrases.notes: If "no" is used in the explanatory role after a noun or na-adjective, there's usually a "na" in front of it. I forgot to explain this, Tae Kim explains the reason on p. 67 or here. Without the "na", it sounds like you'd link the noun to another thing clear from context. Just don't worry about this, without having read this in Tae Kim's book, I'd not even be aware of it.

phrases.reading: きず は だいじょうぶ な の
phrases.lemmaField: 傷 は 大丈夫 だ の
phrases.translation: As for wound, [is it] ok?
phrases.notes:
kizu: wound, injury

If "no" is used in the explanatory role after a noun or na-adjective, there's usually a "na" in front of it. I forgot to explain this, Tae Kim explains the reason on p. 67 or here. Without the "na", it sounds like you'd link the noun to another thing clear from context. Just don't worry about this, without having read this in Tae Kim's book, I'd not even be aware of it.

phrases.reading: これ が つき な の
phrases.lemmaField: これ が 月 だ の
phrases.translation: As for this, [is it the] moon?
phrases.notes:
tsuki: moon

If "no" is used in the explanatory role after a noun or na-adjective, there's usually a "na" in front of it. I forgot to explain this, Tae Kim explains the reason on p. 67 or here. Without the "na", it sounds like you'd link the noun to another thing clear from context. Just don't worry about this, without having read this in Tae Kim's book, I'd not even be aware of it.

phrases.japanese: この道は本当に安全なの
phrases.reading: この みち は ほんとうに あんぜん な の
phrases.lemmaField: この 道 は 本当に 安全 だ の
phrases.romaji: kono michi ha hontouni anzen na no
phrases.translation: [Don't worry, you can take this way home] because as for this road, [it is] really safe.
phrases.notes:
anzen: safety; security

If "no" is used in the explanatory role after a noun or na-adjective, there's usually a "na" in front of it. I forgot to explain this, Tae Kim explains the reason on p. 67 or here. Without the "na", it sounds like you'd link the noun to another thing clear from context. Just don't worry about this, without having read this in Tae Kim's book, I'd not even be aware of it.

phrases.japanese: 大きい願いはダメなの
phrases.reading: おおきい ねがい は だめ な の
phrases.lemmaField: 大きい 願い は ダメ だ の
phrases.romaji: ookii negai ha dame na no
phrases.translation: As for a large wish/favor, is it no good / not allowed? The panda in this series is not only super lazy, but also quite demanding and wants to have a big wish granted by someone.
phrases.notes:
We had "negai" as "wish, hope" before. It can also mean "favor".
dame: no good, not allowed, not possible

phrases.reading: めーる の あいて だれ な の
phrases.lemmaField: メール の 相手 誰 だ の
phrases.romaji: me-ru no aite dare na no
phrases.translation: As for mail partner, who [is it]?
phrases.notes: me-ru: email

phrases.japanese: その気持ちは分かります
phrases.reading: その きもち は わかります
phrases.lemmaField: その 気持ち は 分かる
phrases.translation: As for that feeling [I] understand [it].
phrases.notes:
kimochi: feeling; sensation; mood; state of mind

Remember kimochiii from an earlier card? Now you know where it comes from: kimochi + ii = good feeling / mood.

phrases.reading: こっち に も みち が
phrases.lemmaField: こっち に も 道 が
phrases.translation: They seem to be walking a road that's maybe not in good condition and seem to have talked about this. Then the speaker notes: "Here too road is [bad]".

phrases.japanese: わ私はなぜここにいる
phrases.reading: わ わたし は なぜ ここ に いる
phrases.lemmaField: わ 私 は なぜ ここ に いる
phrases.romaji: wa watashi ha naze koko ni iru
phrases.translation: As for me, why am I here?

phrases.reading: かんたん な ので いい よ
phrases.lemmaField: 簡単 だ ので いい よ なのです なので
phrases.translation: Because it's easy, it's ok -> maybe the guy was asked for a favor and answers: Ok, I do it, but only because it's easy.
phrases.notes: If "no" is used in the explanatory role after a noun or na-adjective, there's usually a "na" in front of it. Tae Kim explains the reason on p. 67 or here. Without the "na", it sounds like you'd link the noun to another thing clear from context.

phrases.japanese: 時間なので失礼します
phrases.reading: じかん な ので しつれいします
phrases.lemmaField: 時間 だ ので 失礼します
phrases.translation: Because [it is] time, I go now, bye.
phrases.notes:
shitsurei: discourtesy; impoliteness​

Reminder: "shitsurei shimasu" is a polite way to say goodbye.

If "no" is used in the explanatory role after a noun or na-adjective, there's usually a "na" in front of it. Tae Kim explains the reason on p. 67 or here. Without the "na", it sounds like you'd link the noun to another thing clear from context.

phrases.reading: むかし から の ともだち な ので
phrases.lemmaField: 昔 から の 友達 だ ので
phrases.romaji: mukashi kara no tomodachi na node
phrases.translation: Because [he is] a friend from long ago [I'm looking forward to meet him].
phrases.notes: If "no" is used in the explanatory role after a noun or na-adjective, there's usually a "na" in front of it. Tae Kim explains the reason on p. 67 or here. Without the "na", it sounds like you'd link the noun to another thing clear from context.

phrases.reading: なあ ほんとうに やる の か
phrases.lemmaField: なあ 本当に やる の か
phrases.translation: [Do we] really do it [physical action]?
phrases.notes: yaru: to do; to undertake; to perform (for physical actions). "yaru" and "suru" have a similar meaning, but you can't just attach "yaru" to nouns the same way as "suru". It is used for physical actions only, read Tae Kim's blog post for more details. Also keep in mind that "yaru" can sound quite rude in certain contexts, this will be explained later.

phrases.reading: これ いつ まで やる の
phrases.lemmaField: これ いつ まで やる の
phrases.translation: This, until when do [we do] it?
phrases.notes: yaru: to do; to undertake; to perform (for physical actions). "yaru" and "suru" have a similar meaning, but you can't just attach "yaru" to nouns the same way as "suru". It is used for physical actions only, read Tae Kim's blog post for more details. Also keep in mind that "yaru" can sound quite rude in certain contexts, this will be explained later.

phrases.reading: あつい のに よく やる な
phrases.lemmaField: 熱い のに よく やる な
phrases.translation: Even though [it is] hot, [he] does well [physical action].
phrases.notes: noni: even though, despite. It can connect two sentences: "sentence 1" noni "sentence 2", the meaning always is: even though "sentence 1", "sentence 2" happened. The same rules as for "node" apply, see following cards.

phrases.japanese: こんなに熱いのにお茶って
phrases.reading: こんなに あつい のに おちゃ って
phrases.lemmaField: こんなに 熱い のに お茶 って
phrases.translation: Even though [it is] this hot, tea?
phrases.notes:
noni: even though, despite. It can connect two sentences: "sentence 1" noni "sentence 2", the meaning always is: even though "sentence 1", "sentence 2" happened. The same rules as for "node" apply, see following cards.
ocha: tea, usually green

Ignore the "tte" here, it means: "you/someone said" It will be covered later in more detail.

phrases.japanese: みんなで頑張ったのに悔しいよ
phrases.reading: みんな で がんばった のに くやしい よ
phrases.lemmaField: みんな で 頑張る のに 悔しい よ
phrases.romaji: minna de ganbatta noni kuyashii yo
phrases.translation: Even though [we] did our best with everybody (i.e. the whole team), it's frustrating. Maybe they lost a match.
phrases.notes:
noni: even though, despite. It can connect two sentences: "sentence 1" noni "sentence 2", the meaning always is: even though "sentence 1", "sentence 2" happened. The same rules as for "node" apply, see following cards.
kuyashii: annoying; frustrating

phrases.japanese: あんなに大きいのに迷子ですって
phrases.reading: あんなに おおきい のに まいご です って
phrases.lemmaField: あんなに 大きい のに 迷子 です って
phrases.romaji: annani ookii noni maigo desu tte
phrases.translation: Even though [he] is that big, [he is] a lost child? -> The person that got lost is actually grown up and his friends pranked him in a department store. The speaker is seeing this person and wonders: Is he really a lost child?
phrases.notes:
noni: even though, despite. It can connect two sentences: "sentence 1" noni "sentence 2", the meaning always is: even though "sentence 1", "sentence 2" happened. The same rules as for "node" apply, see following cards.
maigo: lost child, lost person, stray child

Ignore the "tte" here, it means: "they said"? It will be covered later in more detail.
phrases.source: Ouran High School Host Club (jp eng)

phrases.japanese: 負けたのに偉そうだニャ
phrases.reading: まけた のに えらそう だ にゃ
phrases.lemmaField: 負ける のに 偉そう だ ニャ
phrases.translation: Even though [he] was defeated, [he] looks / seems to feel self-important.
phrases.notes:
noni: even though, despite. It can connect two sentences: "sentence 1" noni "sentence 2", the meaning always is: even though "sentence 1", "sentence 2" happened.
erasou: self-important

Ignore the "nya" part.

phrases.japanese: こんなに近くにいるのにキスもできないよ
phrases.reading: こんなに ちかく に いる のに きす も できない よ
phrases.lemmaField: こんなに 近く に いる のに キス も できる よ
phrases.romaji: konnani chikaku ni iru noni kisu mo dekinai yo
phrases.translation: Even though [they are] that close, [they] can't kiss / don't kiss.
phrases.notes:
noni: even though, despite. It can connect two sentences: "sentence 1" noni "sentence 2", the meaning always is: even though "sentence 1", "sentence 2" happened. 
chikaku: closeness, neighborhood

Ignore the "mo" for now, it's often used in negative sentences like this. It translates to something like "even", I'll add more details later.

phrases.reading: せっかく きた のに
phrases.lemmaField: せっかく 来る のに
phrases.translation: [Noone is here], even though we made an effort and came. "sekkaku" usually means to make some kind of effort. I find this quite hard to translate, it's a weird word ;).
phrases.notes:
Just as for "node", the result that happened "despite something" can be omitted if clear from context.
sekkaku: with trouble; at great pains; specially

phrases.reading: うみ が ちかく に ある のに
phrases.lemmaField: 海 が 近く に ある のに
phrases.romaji: umi ga chikaku ni aru noni
phrases.translation: [You don't go surfing] even though the sea is close?
phrases.notes: Just as for "node", the result that happened "despite something" can be omitted if clear from context.

phrases.reading: おかね ない のに
phrases.lemmaField: お金 ない のに
phrases.translation: [You want to buy it] even though money is not there [i.e. even though you have no money]?
phrases.notes: Just as for "node", the result that happened "despite something" can be omitted if clear from context.

phrases.reading: やくそく した のに
phrases.lemmaField: 約束 する のに
phrases.translation: [He didn't come] even though [he] promised.
phrases.notes: Just as for "node", the result that happened "despite something" can be omitted if clear from context.

phrases.reading: じかん が ない のに
phrases.lemmaField: 時間 が ない のに
phrases.translation: [Why do you complain?! I do it] even though time is not there [even though I don't have time].
phrases.notes: Just as for "node", the result that happened "despite something" can be omitted if clear from context.

phrases.reading: たいせつ な もの な のに
phrases.lemmaField: 大切 だ もの だ のに
phrases.translation: [You lost it] even though it is an important thing?
phrases.notes: If the word before "noni" is a noun or na-adjective, there usually is a "na" in between. Don't worry about the rules too much here.

phrases.reading: がんばった のに
phrases.lemmaField: 頑張る のに
phrases.translation: [I lost] even though [I] tried hard / did my best.

phrases.reading: うまい のに
phrases.lemmaField: うまい のに
phrases.translation: [You don't want to eat this] even though [it is] tasty?

phrases.japanese: よく分からないけど全然いいよ
phrases.reading: よく わからない けど ぜんぜん いい よ
phrases.lemmaField: よく 分かる けど 全然 いい よ
phrases.romaji: yoku wakaranai kedo zenzen ii yo
phrases.translation: [I] don't understand well, but [it] is totally ok.
phrases.notes: kedo: but; it connects two sentences to indicate a contradiction.
phrases.source: Erased - 僕だけがいない街

phrases.japanese: 怖かったけど本当に優しかった
phrases.reading: こわかった けど ほんとうに やさしかった
phrases.lemmaField: 怖い けど 本当に 優しい
phrases.translation: [he looked] scary, but was really gentle / kind.
phrases.notes: kedo: but; it connects two sentences to indicate a contradiction.
phrases.source: Fate Stay Night Unlimited Blade Works S02 (JP Eng)

phrases.japanese: 熱はあるけど大丈夫だよ
phrases.reading: ねつ は ある けど だいじょうぶ だ よ
phrases.lemmaField: 熱 は ある けど 大丈夫 だ よ
phrases.romaji: netsu ha aru kedo daijoubu da yo
phrases.translation: As for temperature / fever, [it] is there, but [this is] ok -> He has temperature, but he's ok. Maybe they're also talking about the cow :D.
phrases.notes: kedo: but; it connects two sentences to indicate a contradiction.

phrases.japanese: 疲れたけど気持ちいいな
phrases.reading: つかれた けど きもちいい な
phrases.lemmaField: 疲れる けど 気持ちいい な
phrases.translation: [I] became tired but [it / something] feels good / is a good feeling.
phrases.notes: kedo: but; it connects two sentences to indicate a contradiction.

phrases.japanese: 疲れたけど楽しかったね
phrases.reading: つかれた けど たのしかった ね
phrases.lemmaField: 疲れる けど 楽しい ね
phrases.translation: [I] became tired but it was enjoyable.
phrases.notes: kedo: but; it connects two sentences to indicate a contradiction.

phrases.japanese: ちょっと遅いけど朝ご飯
phrases.reading: ちょっと おそい けど あさごはん
phrases.lemmaField: ちょっと 遅い けど 朝ご飯
phrases.translation: [It is] a bit late, but [here's] breakfast.

phrases.reading: たべます けど
phrases.lemmaField: 食べる けど
phrases.translation: [I don't like this meal] but I eat.
phrases.notes: If the reason is clear from context, it can be omitted as usual.

phrases.reading: なまえ は おなじ だ けど
phrases.lemmaField: 名前 は 同じ だ けど
phrases.translation: [It looks different] but as for name, [it is] the same.
phrases.notes:
If the reason is clear from context, it can be omitted as usual.

If "kedo" follows a noun or na-adjective, there's usually a "da" in between. This construction is often taught as standalone word (dakedo = but). However, the "but" comes from "kedo" only.

phrases.japanese: あっこれ私のだけど飲む
phrases.reading: あっこれ わたし の だ けど のむ
phrases.lemmaField: あっ 私 の だ けど 飲む
phrases.romaji: akkore watashi no da kedo nomu
phrases.translation: This is mine [i.e. my drink] but [do you want to] drink [it]?
phrases.notes:
If "kedo" follows a noun or na-adjective, there's usually a "da" in between. This construction is often taught as standalone word (dakedo = but). However, the "but" comes from "kedo" only.
Here, the actual noun is omitted (i.e. watashi no drink), but the "da" is still required. If this card is too confusing, just suspend and ignore it.

The "want to" is a consequence of the intonation (this sentence is a question without marker). There are dedicated ways to express "want to", covered later.

phrases.reading: だ けど ここ に いる
phrases.lemmaField: だ けど ここ に いる
phrases.translation: [He said he'd go out ]    ...but [he] is here!
phrases.notes: "da kedo" can also be used to start a sentence: It just means "but" and refers to something said before.

phrases.reading: だ から ごめんなさい
phrases.lemmaField: だ から ごめんなさい
phrases.translation: ...so [I am] sorry.
phrases.notes: Just as "da kedo", "da kara" can also be used to start a sentence: It just means "because" and refers to something said before. Note that this is often taught as standalone word "dakara", but it's in fact da + kara.

phrases.reading: わたし は たのしかった けど
phrases.lemmaField: 私 は 楽しい けど
phrases.translation: [The others didn't like it] but as for me, [it] was enjoyable / fun.
phrases.notes: If the reason is clear from context, it can be omitted as usual.

phrases.reading: おちついた
phrases.lemmaField: 落ち着く
phrases.translation: Did [you] calm down?
phrases.notes: ochitsuku: to calm down

phrases.japanese: 気持ちは分かりますが落ち着いて
phrases.reading: きもち は わかります が おちついて
phrases.lemmaField: 気持ち は 分かる が 落ち着く
phrases.translation: As for [your] feelings [I] understand, but please calm down -> I understand how you feel, but calm down.
phrases.notes:
Instead of "kedo", you may also use "ga" to express "but". It means exactly the same, but is slightly more polite. As a rule of thumb, "ga" is used with teineigo (i.e. -masu forms), while "kedo" is used with plain Japanese. Don't mix this up with the noun-related "ga", it simply means "but" in this case.

"ochitsuite" is the te-form of ochitsuku - to calm down. It is used as imperative here, this will be covered soon.

phrases.japanese: 時間はありませんが落ち着いて
phrases.reading: じかん は ありません が おちついて
phrases.lemmaField: 時間 は ある が 落ち着く
phrases.translation: [We] don't have time, but calm down -> please calm down, even though we have no time (maybe they're in trouble and have to escape).
phrases.notes:
Instead of "kedo", you may also use "ga" to express "but". It means exactly the same, but is slightly more polite. As a rule of thumb, "ga" is used with teineigo (i.e. -masu forms), while "kedo" is used with plain Japanese. Don't mix this up with the noun-related "ga", it simply means "but" in this case.

"ochitsuite" is the te-form of ochitsuku - to calm down. It is used as imperative here, this will be covered soon.

phrases.japanese: かまいませんが大丈夫ですか
phrases.reading: かまいません が だいじょうぶ です か
phrases.lemmaField: かまう が 大丈夫 です か
phrases.translation: [I] don't [mean to] interfere, but [are you] ok? (Maybe the speaker saw some stranger on the street who looks like he could need some help).
phrases.notes:
Instead of "kedo", you may also use "ga" to express "but". It means exactly the same, but is slightly more polite. As a rule of thumb, "ga" is used with teineigo (i.e. -masu forms), while "kedo" is used with plain Japanese. Don't mix this up with the noun-related "ga", it simply means "but" in this case.

kamau: to interfere with, to meddle with (it has multiple meanings, it was introduced as "means to mind, to care about").

phrases.japanese: はい私は大丈夫ですが
phrases.reading: はい わたし は だいじょうぶ です が
phrases.lemmaField: はい 私 は 大丈夫 です が
phrases.romaji: hai watashi ha daijoubu desu ga
phrases.translation: Yes, [I] am ok, but.... [something is still bothering me].
phrases.notes: Instead of "kedo", you may also use "ga" to express "but". If clear from context, a sentence part may be omitted:

phrases.japanese: でもあの子は友達じゃない
phrases.reading: でも あの こ は ともだち じゃない
phrases.lemmaField: でも あの 子 は 友達 じゃ
phrases.romaji: demo ano ko ha tomodachi janai
phrases.translation: ...but as for that kid, [it] is not friend.
phrases.notes: ko: kid, child (it's short for kodomo, we already had this before).

phrases.japanese: 私は構いませんがあの子たちは
phrases.reading: わたし は かまいません が あの こたち は
phrases.lemmaField: 私 は 構う が あの 子たち は
phrases.romaji: watashi ha kamaimasen ga ano kotachi ha
phrases.translation: As for me [I] don't [mean to] interfere, but as for these kids... [should they really be doing this?!]
phrases.grammarNote: The "ga" is a bit slurry here.
phrases.notes: The "ga" is hard to notice here.

phrases.reading: きれい だ し やさしい し
phrases.lemmaField: キレイ だ し 優しい し
phrases.translation: [I like her] because [she's] pretty and kind [among other things].
phrases.notes:
When you want to provide an (incomplete) list of reasons for something, you can use "shi". Simply append it to the sentence / relative clause. If the clause ends on a noun or na-adjective, there's usually a "da" before the "shi". We already this on earlier cards, Tae Kim officially introduces it in the "compound sentences"-chapter. Since the list of reasons is usually incomplete, I use "among other things" in the translation.

Remark: Quite often, "shi" is appended to every relative clause in the list of incomplete reasons, just as in this example. As we will see however, this is not always the case.

phrases.japanese: 暑いしそれに疲れたわよ
phrases.reading: あつい し それ に つかれた わ よ
phrases.lemmaField: 暑い し それ に 疲れる わ よ それに
phrases.romaji: atsui shi sore ni tsukareta wa yo
phrases.translation: [I don't like it here in this forest, because it's] hot among other things... and besides this [I] became tired.
phrases.notes:
soreni: besides, in addition

When you want to list multiple reasons for something, you can append "shi" to (each) sentence/clause. Note that this usually is an incomplete list of reasons, hence the "among other things" in the translation.
Remark: The additional "sore ni" here caused some confusion, because it adds another reason why the speaker wants to leave the forest. Tae Kim and other resources however, point out that the "shi" must be added after every reason (which is wrong). Here, you could interpret this as two distinct sentences, joined together by "sore ni" - this is just what it does: The "atsui shi" is one out of a few reasons the speaker does not being in the forest. And then, in addition to this, she became tired. It's from Hyouka, ep. 8 around 8:00, if you want to check.

phrases.japanese: 嘘もつかないし悪いこともしない
phrases.reading: うそ も つかない し わるい こと も しない
phrases.lemmaField: 嘘 も つく し 悪い こと も する
phrases.romaji: uso mo tsukanai shi warui koto mo shinai
phrases.translation: [You're a good person because you] not only do not lie, but [you] also do not do any bad things.
phrases.notes: If "shi" is used like this, it can also be translated as "not only x, but also y". Have a look at the references, they are more exhaustive as Tae Kim's guide in this case. Note that the general meaning of an incomplete list of reasons also applies here, but the "shi" is not appended to every sentence as explained in some resources.

phrases.japanese: それは私の問題だしさ
phrases.reading: それ は わたし の もんだい だ し さ
phrases.lemmaField: それ は 私 の 問題 だ し さ
phrases.romaji: sore ha watashi no mondai da shi sa
phrases.translation: [You don't need to help / do this, because it's] my problem [among other things].
phrases.notes:
When you want to list multiple reasons for something, you can append "shi" to every sentence. Again, Tae Kim's explanation of this topic is a bit superficial, if you want to know more, have a look at the refs.

"sa" is a sentence ending particle that indicates assertion. It already appeared on an earlier card, where I recommended to ignore it, which you can also do here. However, it's usually easy to understand, read more here if you are interested.

phrases.japanese: 今日は天気もいいし楽しいよさあ
phrases.reading: きょう は てんき も いい し たのしい よ さあ
phrases.lemmaField: 今日 は 天気 も いい し 楽しい よ さあ
phrases.romaji: kyou ha tenki mo ii shi tanoshii yo saa
phrases.translation: [Let's go to the sea because] as for today, not only the weather is good, but it's also fun!
phrases.notes: My translations of "shi" focused a bit too hard on Tae Kim's explanation (one out of many reasons). If used like this, I'd rather translate it as "not only X, but also Y" - see additional refs.
phrases.source: Saiki Kusuo no Psi Nan S1 (斉木楠雄のΨ難 第1期)

phrases.reading: うまい し はやい し
phrases.lemmaField: うまい し 早い し
phrases.translation: [He's] skilled and fast [among other things].
phrases.notes: shi: marks incomplete list of reasons for something. Here, it's appended to every reason, but this is not always the case.

phrases.reading: だれも いない し さむい し
phrases.lemmaField: 誰も いる し 寒い し
phrases.translation: [I want to go home because] noone is here and it is cold [among other things].
phrases.notes: shi: marks incomplete list of reasons for something. Here, it's appended to every reason, but this is not always the case.
phrases.source: The World God Only Knows S3 (jp eng)

phrases.japanese: 怖いし寂しいし悲しいわ
phrases.reading: こわい し さびしい し かなしい わ
phrases.lemmaField: 怖い し 寂しい し 悲しい わ
phrases.romaji: kowai shi sabishii shi kanashii wa
phrases.translation: [I want to go home because it's] scary, lonely and miserable [here].
phrases.notes:
sabishii: lonely; lonesome; solitary
kanashii: sad; miserable

shi: marks incomplete list of reasons for something. Here, it's appended to every reason, but this is not always the case.

phrases.reading: あかるい し おもしろい よ ね
phrases.lemmaField: 明るい し 面白い よ ね
phrases.translation: [I like her because she's] not only cheerful but also interesting.
phrases.notes:
akarui: cheerful, bright (of a colour)

shi: marks incomplete list of reasons for something. Here, it's used for emphasis (not only, but also).

phrases.japanese: あなた美人だしとても好きよ
phrases.reading: あなた びじん だ し とても すき よ
phrases.lemmaField: あなた 美人 だ し とても 好き よ
phrases.romaji: anata bijin da shi totemo suki yo
phrases.translation: I like you very much [because you're a] beautiful woman [among other things].
phrases.notes:
bijin: beautiful woman

shi: marks incomplete list of reasons for something. Here, only one out of several reasons is given.

phrases.japanese: ねえ暑いし何か飲まない
phrases.reading: ねえ あつい し なにか のまない
phrases.lemmaField: ねえ 暑い し 何か 飲む
phrases.translation: It's hot [among other things], [why] don't we drink something?
phrases.notes: shi: marks incomplete list of reasons for something. Here, only one out of several reasons is given.
phrases.source: JoJos Bizarre Adventure 黄金の風 (26-39)

phrases.reading: でも おれ じゅく ある し な
phrases.lemmaField: でも 俺 塾 ある し な
phrases.romaji: demo ore juku aru shi na
phrases.translation: [I can't go because among other things] cram school is there -> I have to go to cram school.
phrases.notes:
juku: cram school; private tutoring school. The wikipedia article on Japanese cram schools is interesting, they are very common in Japan.

shi: marks incomplete list of reasons for something. Here, only one out of several reasons is given.
phrases.source: Kokoro ga Sakebitagatterunda (Anthem of the Heart)

phrases.japanese: 僕はお前を許さないしお前は僕を許さない
phrases.reading: ぼく は おまえ を ゆるさない し おまえ は ぼく を ゆるさない
phrases.lemmaField: 僕 は お前 を 許す し お前 は 僕 を 許す
phrases.romaji: boku ha omae wo yurusanai shi omae ha boku wo yurusanai
phrases.translation: [We'll continue to fight because] I don't forgive you and you don't forgive me [among other things].
phrases.notes: yurusu: to forgive; to pardon

phrases.reading: ここ きもちいい し さ
phrases.lemmaField: ここ 気持ちいい し さ
phrases.translation: [I like this place. The view is great and] it feels good [here, among other things].

phrases.japanese: 全然嬉しくないし楽しくない
phrases.reading: ぜんぜん うれしくない し たのしくない
phrases.lemmaField: 全然 うれしい し 楽しい
phrases.translation: [Something was] totally not joyful and fun.
phrases.notes:
ureshii: happy; glad; joyful
tanoshii: enjoyable; fun

phrases.japanese: 知らないし興味もないよ
phrases.reading: しらない し きょうみ も ない よ
phrases.lemmaField: 知る し 興味 も ない よ
phrases.romaji: shiranai shi kyoumi mo nai yo
phrases.translation: [I can't help you because I] not only don't know anything [about it] but also have no interest [in this].
phrases.notes: kyoumi: interest in something, curiosity

phrases.japanese: でももう飽きたし眠いわ
phrases.reading: でも もう あきた し ねむい わ
phrases.lemmaField: でも もう 飽きる し 眠い わ
phrases.romaji: demo mou akita shi nemui wa
phrases.translation: [You really want to continue?] But [I] not only lost interest already but also am sleepy.
phrases.notes:
akiru: to get tired of; to lose interest in

The "wa" in the end is a female sentence ending particle. The use varies around regions and is a bit hard to explain - just ignore it or read the ref. Here's Tofugu's summary: "わ usually follows a statement that expresses your realization of something, reflecting your view or attitude toward a situation or event. It indicates that you came to a conclusion, felt a certain way, or are making a sudden observation based on personal experience."

phrases.reading: くさい し ね
phrases.lemmaField: 臭い し ね
phrases.translation: [I don't like this place] it's stinky, among other things.
phrases.notes: kusai: stinking; smelly

phrases.reading: なに し に きた の
phrases.lemmaField: なに する に くる の
phrases.translation: Do you remember this sentence? Reminder: The "shi" here has a different meaning, it's the nominalized form of "suru - to do" and means: What did you come here for?
phrases.notes: You get the nominalization of a verb by omitting the "masu" part in teineigo.

phrases.reading: ないた か
phrases.lemmaField: 泣く か
phrases.translation: [You] cried?
phrases.notes: naku: to cry

phrases.reading: はい なきません
phrases.lemmaField: はい 泣く
phrases.translation: Yes, [I] don't cry.
phrases.notes:
naku: to cry

The guy told the girl not to cry. Sounds like a weird conversation, but I need the word "naku" for one of the next cards...

phrases.reading: こい する の
phrases.lemmaField: 恋 する の
phrases.translation: [You] fell in love?
phrases.notes:
koi: romantic love
koi suru: to fall in love (not: to make love!)

phrases.reading: さいご に わらう の は
phrases.lemmaField: 最後 に 笑う の は
phrases.translation: As for the one who laughs last [it's probably the speaker].

phrases.reading: しっぱい した
phrases.lemmaField: 失敗 する
phrases.translation: [I] failed / made a mistake.
phrases.notes: shippai: failure; mistake

phrases.japanese: この仕事に失敗は許されない
phrases.reading: この しごと に しっぱい は ゆるされない
phrases.lemmaField: この 仕事 に 失敗 は 許す
phrases.romaji: kono shigoto ni shippai ha yurusarenai
phrases.translation: This job does not forgive mistakes (looks like they are working on a dangerous construction site).
phrases.grammarNote: yurusarenai is negative passive tense. Ignore it for now and replace it with "yurusenai - don't forgive, don't allow".

phrases.reading: なんで わらう の
phrases.lemmaField: なんで 笑う の
phrases.translation: Why [do you] laugh?
phrases.notes: The "nande" is hard to understand. If you didn't use headphones up to this point, now is probably a good time to try, they make listening comprehension much easier...

phrases.reading: わたし しっぱい した か な
phrases.lemmaField: 私 失敗 する か な
phrases.translation: I failed / made a mistake, didn't I?

phrases.japanese: 皆さんは最近失敗をしましたか
phrases.reading: みなさん は さいきん しっぱい を しました か
phrases.lemmaField: 皆さん は 最近 失敗 を する か みなさん
phrases.romaji: minasan ha saikin shippai wo shimashita ka
phrases.translation: As for everybody [you, the audience], recently made a mistake / failed? -> How about you? Did you recently make a mistake?

phrases.reading: なぜ にげる
phrases.lemmaField: なぜ 逃げる
phrases.translation: Why [do you] run away?
phrases.notes: nigeru: to escape; to run away

phrases.reading: にげる の よ ふたり で
phrases.lemmaField: 逃げる の よ ２人 だ
phrases.translation: [We] escape! With the two of you.

phrases.japanese: でもその子も私から逃げた
phrases.reading: でも その こ も わたし から にげた
phrases.lemmaField: でも その 子 も 私 から 逃げる
phrases.romaji: demo sono ko mo watashi kara nigeta
phrases.translation: [A long time ago I had a single friend] but that kid also ran away from me.

phrases.japanese: みんなたぶん逃げたよね
phrases.reading: みんな たぶん にげた よ ね
phrases.lemmaField: みんな たぶん 逃げる よ ね
phrases.translation: [They] all escaped, maybe.

phrases.japanese: もちろん逃げますよね
phrases.reading: もちろん にげます よ ね
phrases.lemmaField: もちろん 逃げる よ ね
phrases.translation: [We] escape, of course.
phrases.notes: mochiron: of course; certainly; naturally

phrases.japanese: 笑ったり泣いたり恋したりするの
phrases.reading: わらったり ないたり こいしたり する の
phrases.lemmaField: 笑う 泣く 恋 する の
phrases.translation: [I want to return to earth] because [there I can] do things like laughing, crying and falling in love [just like other girls].
phrases.notes:
You can connect a list multiple actions / verbs among a potentially larger list using the pattern "-tari + suru": Put the verb to past tense, attach "ri" and end the sentence with suru (and maybe a sentence ending particle like in this example). The meaning becomes: I did this, that and a few other things.

The tense is determined by the last "suru". The difference to the te-form is, that the "-tari + suru"-pattern lists multiple things among others in no particular order. If you said: "waratte naite koi suru", you'd to these things in exactly this order.

The difference to "shi" is that "-tari suru" applies only to verbs and not necessarily states reasons.

phrases.japanese: 一度失敗して泣いたり逃げたりすると
phrases.reading: いちど しっぱい して ないたり にげたり する と
phrases.lemmaField: 一度 失敗 する 泣く 逃げる する と
phrases.romaji: ichido shippai shite naitari nigetari suru to
phrases.translation: This is a nice example of multiple "compound constructors" in one sentence (-te form and -tari suru), it means: If you fail once and cry and run away (among other things)...[it's ok].
phrases.grammarNote: The trailing "to" means "if" in this case. What follows after is omitted, just ignore it for now.
phrases.notes: You can connect a list multiple actions / verbs among a potentially larger list using the pattern "-tari + suru": Put the verb to past tense, attach "ri" and end the sentence with suru (and maybe a sentence ending particle like in this example). The meaning becomes: I did this, that and a few other things.

phrases.japanese: 僕は彼女が泣いたり困ったりするのが好きじゃない
phrases.reading: ぼく は かのじょ が ないたり こまったり する の が すき じゃない
phrases.lemmaField: 僕 は 彼女 が 泣くたり 困る する の が 好き じゃ
phrases.romaji: boku ha kanojo ga naitari komattari suru no ga suki janai
phrases.translation: As for me, I don't like it if she cries and is in trouble (among other things).
phrases.notes: You can connect a list multiple actions / verbs among a potentially larger list using the pattern "-tari + suru": Put the verb to past tense, attach "ri" and end the sentence with suru (and maybe a sentence ending particle like in this example). The meaning becomes: I did this, that and a few other things.

phrases.japanese: おいしいお店があったりする
phrases.reading: おいしい おみせ が あったり する
phrases.lemmaField: おいしい お店 が ある する
phrases.translation: [I like to go there, because there's a] tasty shop there [among other things] -> It means a store offering tasty food.
phrases.notes:
mise: store; shop (with polite o-prefix)

The "-tari suru"-construction does not need multiple verbs in this form as in the previous examples. You'll often have sentences like this with just one verb ending on -tari. This adds the meaning of "among other things" or "...and the like". It's imply a single thing out of many more.
Remark: Here, we have the -tari suru form of "aru", which means: to be there, among other things.

phrases.japanese: 何か予定あったりするの
phrases.reading: なんか よてい あったり する の
phrases.lemmaField: 何か 予定 ある する の
phrases.translation: Do you have any kind of plans [and maybe other things in mind]?
phrases.notes:
yotei: plans; arrangement; schedule
nanka: something like ...; things like (casual of nanika)

The "-tari suru"-construction does not need multiple verbs in this form as in the previous examples. You'll often have sentences like this with just one verb ending on -tari. This adds the meaning of "among other things" or "...and the like". It's imply a single thing out of many more.

phrases.reading: かるく なったり する
phrases.lemmaField: 軽い なる する
phrases.translation: [Something] becomes light [among other things].
phrases.notes:
karui: light, not heavy

The "-tari suru"-construction does not need multiple verbs in this form as in the previous examples. You'll often have sentences like this with just one verb ending on -tari. This adds the meaning of "among other things" or "...and the like". It's imply a single thing out of many more.
phrases.source: ダンベル何キロ持てる (dumbbell) 1-6

phrases.reading: ねぼう したり する
phrases.lemmaField: 寝坊 する する
phrases.translation: [I am often late because I] oversleep [among other things].
phrases.notes:
nebou: oversleeping (noun)

Note the interesting noun-suru-suru construction here: nebou suru = to oversleep conjugated to -tari suru.

phrases.japanese: 私明日いなかったりする
phrases.reading: わたし あした いなかったり する
phrases.lemmaField: 私 明日 いる する あした
phrases.translation: I am not there tomorrow [among other things - they are talking about going to a party. Terrace house boys x girls next door, S7 after 19:30].
phrases.notes:
ashita: tomorrow

The "suru" in the end sounds like a "s".

Remark: We don't have past tense here, it's -tari suru - incomplete listing.
phrases.source: Terrace House-Boys x Girls Next Door

phrases.japanese: お家を忘れたりしませんよね
phrases.reading: おうち を わすれたり しません よ ね
phrases.lemmaField: お家 を 忘れるたり する よ ね
phrases.romaji: ouchi wo wasuretari shimasen yo ne
phrases.translation: [I] won't forget my home.
phrases.notes:
uchi: one's house; one's home; one's family (with polite o-prefix)

In this example you see how the conjugations work for "-tari suru"-constructions: The last suru is inflected.

phrases.japanese: 私たちは逃げたりしません
phrases.reading: わたしたち は にげたり しません
phrases.lemmaField: 私たち は 逃げるたり する
phrases.translation: As for us, [we] don't run away.
phrases.notes: In this example you see how the conjugations work for "-tari suru"-constructions: The last suru is inflected.

phrases.reading: これ たべたり
phrases.lemmaField: これ 食べるたり
phrases.translation: [I] eat this [among other things].
phrases.notes:
The "suru" is often omitted in casual conversations.

The speaker lists stuff she's doing at the moment.

phrases.reading: びーる のん だり
phrases.lemmaField: ビール 飲む だり
phrases.translation: [I] drink beer [and so on / and do other things].
phrases.notes:
The "suru" is often omitted in casual conversations.

The speaker lists stuff she's doing at the moment.

phrases.reading: きょう は たのしかった な
phrases.lemmaField: 今日 は 楽しい な
phrases.translation: As for today, [it] was fun.
phrases.grammarNote: This one and the next 3 cards belong together.

phrases.reading: でも ひょっとして
phrases.lemmaField: でも ひょっとして
phrases.translation: But maybe...
phrases.grammarNote: This one and the next 2 cards belong together.
phrases.notes: hyottoshite: by any chance; by some chance; maybe

phrases.reading: また ゆめ だったり とか
phrases.lemmaField: また 夢 だ とか
phrases.translation: ...[it] was a dream again [and the like...]
phrases.grammarNote: This one and the next card belong together.
phrases.notes: The "-tari suru"-form also works for the state of being (da), with exactly the same rules, it's da -> datta (past) -> dattari. However, the "suru" is again missing here.

phrases.reading: ゆめ じゃない
phrases.lemmaField: 夢 じゃない
phrases.translation: The first word is supposed to mean "atsui", sounds like she's taking a hot shower and finally realizes, that she's not dreaming.

phrases.japanese: それは友達だったり好きな人だったり
phrases.reading: それ は ともだち だったり すき な ひと だったり
phrases.lemmaField: それ は 友達 だ 好き だ 人 だ
phrases.romaji: sore ha tomodachi dattari suki na hito dattari
phrases.translation: As for that... [he's] a friend, a person [I] like [among other things].
phrases.notes: The "-tari suru"-form also works for the state of being (da), with exactly the same rules, it's da -> datta (past) -> dattari. The "suru" is again missing here.

phrases.japanese: かかわいかったりするの
phrases.reading: か かわいかったり する の
phrases.lemmaField: か かわいい する の
phrases.translation: [You think it/someone is] cute and all that? -> Answer see next card.
phrases.grammarNote: The next card and this one belong together.
phrases.notes: "-tari suru" also works for i-adjectives, even though this is less common than for verbs.

phrases.reading: はい かわいい です が
phrases.lemmaField: はい かわいい です が ですが
phrases.translation: Yes, cute but... (the "but" comes from "ga", just as we learned before).

phrases.reading: だめ だめ わたし を ころして
phrases.lemmaField: ダメ ダメ 私 を 殺す
phrases.translation: 'No! Don't [go away]. Kill me!'
phrases.notes: Here, the speaker is telling the other person in the image to kill her.

phrases.reading: だめ です よ おさけ は
phrases.lemmaField: ダメ です よ お酒 は
phrases.translation: No good, alcoholic beverage [I mean].

phrases.japanese: それはダメなことなのか
phrases.reading: それ は だめ な こと な の か
phrases.lemmaField: それ は ダメ だ こと だ の か
phrases.romaji: sore ha dame na koto na no ka
phrases.translation: As for that, [is it a] no good-thing? -> It this something [someone] shouldn't do?
phrases.notes: "dame" is used within a broad context to express that something is not good and maybe should not be done. We'll learn some more important use cases later.

phrases.japanese: ダメです兄は渡しません
phrases.reading: だめ です あに は わたしません
phrases.lemmaField: ダメ です 兄 は 渡す
phrases.translation: No good! As for [my] older brother, [I] don't hand [him] over.
phrases.grammarNote: The black haired girl says this, look what she's doing.
phrases.notes:
watasu: to hand over

Note again that the thing to be handed over is clear from context. Seems like the red haired girl wants to go out with the guy and the black haired girl is holding him (older brother) back. Depending on the context it could also mean that they're talking about some item and the girl explains: Brother doesn't hand it over.

phrases.japanese: ダメだ全然集中できない
phrases.reading: だめ だ ぜんぜん しゅうちゅう できない
phrases.lemmaField: ダメ だ 全然 集中 できる
phrases.translation: No good / impossible, [I] totally can't concentrate.
phrases.notes: shuuchuu: concentration, focusing

phrases.reading: もも うそ は だめ よ
phrases.lemmaField: もも 嘘 は ダメ よ
phrases.translation: Momo, as for a lie, [it's] no good -> don't lie, Momo!
phrases.source: ももへの手紙(A Letter to Momo)

phrases.japanese: ダメこの恋は叶わない
phrases.reading: だめ この こい は かなわない
phrases.lemmaField: ダメ この 恋 は 叶う
phrases.translation: No good, as for this love, [it] doesn't come true (maybe someone doesn't love her back).
phrases.notes: kanau: to come true (of a wish, prayer, etc.); to be realized; to be fulfilled
phrases.source: さよなら絶望先生 (Sayonara, Zetsubou-Sensei)

phrases.japanese: ごめん甘い物ダメだった俺
phrases.reading: ごめん あまいもの だめ だった おれ
phrases.lemmaField: ごめん 甘い物 ダメ だ 俺
phrases.translation: Sorry, sweets were no good (for me). Maybe he spat them out and apologizes for that.
phrases.notes: amaimono (amai + mono): sweet things, sweets
phrases.source: The Daily Lives of High School Boys (EP 1-12)

phrases.japanese: 駄目だ私にはできない
phrases.reading: だめ だ わたし に は できない
phrases.lemmaField: 駄目 だ わたし に は できる
phrases.romaji: dame da watashi ni ha dekinai
phrases.translation: It's no good, [it's something] I can't do.
phrases.notes: Note the "ni + ha" particle combination. We already had this on a separate card before, the sentence was "bokutachi ni ha wakaru". Technically, it marks "watashi" as target of "dekiru". This means, that "not being able to do something" is limited to "watashi" in this case. They're talking about marrying someone here and the speaker can't do that for whatever reason. Read more on this here.

phrases.reading: おかし おいしい
phrases.lemmaField: お菓子 おいしい
phrases.translation: okashi: sweets, confections, candy
phrases.notes: This is a different word for sweets, it's more specific than the "amaimono" of the last card. Note that particles are missing again (e.g. okashi ha/ga).

phrases.japanese: あのね私は先生なのよ
phrases.reading: あの ね わたし は せんせい な の よ
phrases.lemmaField: あの ね 私 は 先生 だ の よ
phrases.romaji: ano ne watashi ha sensei na no yo
phrases.translation: Well, as for me, [I am your] teacher.  (conversation continues on next card)
phrases.grammarNote: This card and the next belong together.
phrases.notes:
The speaker is the teacher of some kids, who invited her to join their all girls gossip meeting. She wants to refuse and gives the reason here.

Remember: The explanatory "no" requires a "na" before it, if it's used together with a noun, otherwise it would imply there's an attribute / possession linked to the teacher, that's clear from context and thus omitted.

phrases.japanese: ねえ少しだけお菓子もありますよ
phrases.reading: ねえ すこし だけ おかし も あります よ
phrases.lemmaField: ねえ 少し だけ お菓子 も ある よ
phrases.romaji: nee sukoshi dake okashi mo arimasu yo
phrases.translation: Come on [teacher], only a little bit, sweets are there, too!
phrases.notes: dake: only

phrases.japanese: 何のことだか分からない
phrases.reading: なん の こと だ か わからない
phrases.lemmaField: 何 の こと だ か 分かる
phrases.romaji: nan no koto da ka wakaranai
phrases.translation: I have no idea what [you are talking] about. -> Here, the conversation revolves around the question of what a certain thing or matter actually is. The speaker doesn't understand and says: I don't understand the question of "what matter is it?".
phrases.notes:
A relative clause (i.e. a subsentence embedded into a larger sentence) ending on "ka" allows to talk about a certain question.

Relative clause: "nan no koto da ka - what matter is it?"
"Main" sentence: "wakaranai - I don't understand".

Note that "wakaru" means to understand or comprehend something. To just "know" something is "shiru" in Japanese, keep this in mind for the following examples.

phrases.japanese: どこに行ったか分かります
phrases.reading: どこ に いった か わかります
phrases.lemmaField: どこ に 行く か 分かる
phrases.translation: Here, the conversation revolves around the question of where someone went, the speaker asks: Do you understand where he went?
phrases.notes:
A relative clause (i.e. a subsentence embedded into a larger sentence) ending on "ka" allows to talk about a certain question.

Relative clause: "doko ni itta ka - where did [he] go?"
"Main" sentence: "wakarimasu - do you know?" (Listen to the intonation, it's a question).

Note that "wakaru" means to understand or comprehend something. To just "know" something is "shiru" in Japanese, keep this in mind for the following examples.

phrases.japanese: 今はどこにいるか分かんねぇけど
phrases.reading: いま は どこ に いる か わかんねぇ けど
phrases.lemmaField: 今 は どこ に いる か 分かる けど
phrases.romaji: ima ha doko ni iru ka wakannee kedo
phrases.translation: Here, the conversation revolves around the question of where someone is. The speaker says: [I know where he was yesterday] but I don't understand where he is now.
phrases.grammarNote: wakaranee - slang for "wakaranai"
phrases.notes:
A relative clause (i.e. a subsentence embedded into a larger sentence) ending on "ka" allows to talk about a certain question.

Relative clause: "ima ha doko ni iru ka - as for now, where is [he]?"
"Main" sentence: "wakaranai kedo - but I don't understand".

phrases.japanese: 何をしたか分かりますか
phrases.reading: なに を した か わかります か
phrases.lemmaField: 何 を する か 分かる か
phrases.romaji: nani wo shita ka wakarimasu ka
phrases.translation: Here, the conversation revolves around the question of what someone did. The speaker wants to understand and asks: Do you understand what [he] did? Maybe someone did a complicated task.
phrases.notes:
A relative clause (i.e. a subsentence embedded into a larger sentence) ending on "ka" allows to talk about a certain question.

Relative clause: "nani wo shita ka - what did [he] do?"
"Main" sentence: "wakarimasu ka - do you know?"

Do you get the pattern? The essence is this: When you want to talk about a certain question, you explicitly include it as relative clause (i.e. subsentence). I add more sentences, but keep the explanations shorter on the next cards. If you need more explanations, please drop me a message using the question links.

phrases.japanese: 何があったか分かるよな
phrases.reading: なに が あった か わかる よ な
phrases.lemmaField: 何 が ある か 分かる よ な
phrases.romaji: nani ga atta ka wakaru yo na
phrases.translation: You understand what happened, don't you?!
phrases.notes:
Relative clause: "nani ga atta ka - what was there? what happened?"
"Main" sentence: "wakaru yo na - you know, don't you!?"

phrases.japanese: 俺が誰だか分かったか
phrases.reading: おれ が だれ だ か わかった か
phrases.lemmaField: 俺 が 誰 だ か 分かる か
phrases.romaji: ore ga dare da ka wakatta ka
phrases.translation: Did [you] understand who I am?

phrases.japanese: どうしていいのか分からない
phrases.reading: どうして いい の か わからない
phrases.lemmaField: どうして いい の か 分かる
phrases.translation: I don't understand why [that] is ok.

phrases.japanese: どこにいるか分かるか
phrases.reading: どこ に いる か わかる か
phrases.lemmaField: どこ に いる か 分かる か
phrases.romaji: doko ni iru ka wakaru ka
phrases.translation: Do [you] understand where [we] are? Sounds like they are in some special place.

phrases.japanese: どこに向かうのか分からないけど
phrases.reading: どこ に むかう の か わからない けど
phrases.lemmaField: どこ に 向かう の か 分かる けど
phrases.romaji: doko ni mukau no ka wakaranai kedo
phrases.translation: [I know where he is now], but [I] don't understand where [he] heads towards.
phrases.notes: mukau: to go towards; to head towards

phrases.japanese: 自分が何をするか分からないかな
phrases.reading: じぶん が なに を する か わからない か な
phrases.lemmaField: 自分 が 何 を する か 分かる か な
phrases.romaji: jibun ga nani wo suru ka wakaranai ka na
phrases.translation: [I just] don't understand what [I] would do myself [if they were dating].
phrases.grammarNote: Ignore the "ka na" ending for now.
phrases.notes:
We already had "jibun" on earlier cards, it has a funny dictionary definition: "myself; yourself; oneself; himself; herself". It refers to "someone self" in general.

Ignore the "ka na" ending for now.

phrases.japanese: 何があったか知らないけどさあ
phrases.reading: なに が あった か しらない けど さあ
phrases.lemmaField: 何 が ある か 知る けど さあ
phrases.romaji: nani ga atta ka shiranai kedo saa
phrases.translation: [She behaves weird, ] but [I] don't know what happened.
phrases.notes: A sentence with "shiru - to know":

phrases.japanese: 何で興味持ったのか知らないけど
phrases.reading: なんで きょうみ もった の か しらない けど
phrases.lemmaField: 何で 興味 持つ の か 知る けど
phrases.romaji: nande kyoumi motta no ka shiranai kedo
phrases.translation: ... but I don't know why [he] had interest [in something].
phrases.notes:
kyoumi: interest
motsu: to carry
kyoumi wo motsu: to have interest in something

phrases.japanese: みんなどこに行ったか知らないかな
phrases.reading: みんな どこ に いった か しらない か な
phrases.lemmaField: みんな どこ に 行く か 知る か な
phrases.romaji: minna doko ni itta ka shiranai ka na
phrases.translation: [You] don't know where the others went, do you?

phrases.japanese: いつだったか忘れたけど
phrases.reading: いつ だった か わすれた けど
phrases.lemmaField: いつ だ か 忘れる けど
phrases.translation: [I know what happened] but [I] forgot when it was.

phrases.reading: なに を かんがえて いる の か
phrases.lemmaField: 何 を 考える いる の か
phrases.romaji: nani wo kangaete iru no ka
phrases.translation: What are [you] thinking?!
phrases.notes: Here, we have kangaete (from kangaeru: to think) + iru (to be, to exist). This combination does not translate to "I think and I am", but is used to express an enduring state or action (I am thinking), so the sentence means:

phrases.reading: なに を して いる
phrases.lemmaField: 何 を する いる
phrases.translation: What are [you] doing?
phrases.notes: verb in te-form + iru: Enduring state or action, similar to the English "-ing" form. It is used for both animate and inanimate things.

phrases.reading: ここ で なに を して いる
phrases.lemmaField: ここ で 何 を する いる
phrases.romaji: koko de nani wo shite iru
phrases.translation: What are [you] doing here?

phrases.reading: これ を しって いる か
phrases.lemmaField: これ を 知る いる か
phrases.translation: [Do you] know this?
phrases.notes:
It's important to keep in mind that "-te iru" describes not only ongoing actions, but also ongoing states. States often do not directly translate to the English progressive forms. This is covered on the following cards, also refer to Tae Kim's explanation.

"To know" refers to the ongoing state of knowing something. So in Japanese, the term "shitte iru" is quite common, while in English you'd rather not say "I'm knowing this".

Note how similar the te-forms of suru - shite and shiru - shitte sound, it's easy to mix them up when listening to something.

phrases.reading: ここ に かいて ある
phrases.lemmaField: ここ に 書く ある
phrases.translation: [Something] is written here [the process of writing is completed and now the everything stays to be written down].
phrases.notes:
Here, we have kaite (from kaku: to write) + aru. This combination describes the state after a certain action was completed, not the ongoing action itself. The sentence means:

Using "te iru" instead (koko ni kaite imasu) the sentence would mean: The writing is ongoing at the moment, someone "is writing".
Something I found a bit confusing here is the fact that both "-te iru" and "-te aru" describe states. The difference is that "-te aru" describes the state after an action completed and usually translates to the English passive voice (writing vs. was written).
