phrases.notes: hodo: extent; degree; limit.

phrases.japanese: あれほどの元気はありませんよ
phrases.reading: あれ ほど の げんき は ありません よ
phrases.lemmaField: あれ ほど の 元気 は ある よ
phrases.romaji: are hodo no genki ha arimasen yo
phrases.translation: To this-degree lively / healthy / well is not there -> I am not that genki.
phrases.notes: hodo: extent; degree; limit.

phrases.reading: わらえる ほど に ね
phrases.lemmaField: 笑える ほど に ね
phrases.translation: [I was tasty] to a can-laugh extend.
phrases.notes:
hodo: extent; degree; limit.

Remark: The "ni" directs what is hidden in the previous sentence of the conversation towards "waraeru hodo":  The ramen at this shop was sooo good, to the extend I could laugh.

phrases.reading: しつれい に も ほど が ある
phrases.lemmaField: 失礼 に も 程 が ある
phrases.romaji: shitsurei ni mo hodo ga aru
phrases.translation: For impoliteness, there's a limit!
phrases.notes: shitsurei: discourtesy; impoliteness​

phrases.reading: ほんとうに たかい です わ ね
phrases.lemmaField: 本当に 高い です わ ね
phrases.translation: This is really high.
phrases.grammarNote: Look where they are standing.
phrases.notes: takai: high / expensive

phrases.japanese: あなたが高いのは聞いています
phrases.reading: あなた が たかい の は きいて います
phrases.lemmaField: あなた が 高い の は 聞く いる
phrases.romaji: anata ga takai no ha kiite imasu
phrases.translation: I heard that you are expensive (could also mean: tall)

phrases.reading: 30めーとる の たかさ から
phrases.lemmaField: 30メートル の 高い から
phrases.translation: [This has] a height of 30 meters.
phrases.grammarNote: Ignore the number in the beginning (sanju - 30).
phrases.notes:
takasa: height

By replacing the "i" of an i-adjective with "sa" you nominalize it (we already had oishii -> oishisa before).
phrases.source: Saiki Kusuo no Psi Nan S1 (斉木楠雄のΨ難 第1期)

phrases.japanese: 熱はまだあるじゃないか
phrases.reading: ねつ は まだ ある じゃない か
phrases.lemmaField: 熱 は まだ ある じゃ か
phrases.romaji: netsu ha mada aru janai ka
phrases.translation: As for temperature / fever, isn't it still there?-> [You want to go out, but] don't you still have temperature?
phrases.notes: mada: still (don't mix it up with mata - again)

phrases.japanese: めんまはまだ帰ってこない
phrases.reading: めんま は まだ かえって こない
phrases.lemmaField: めんま は まだ 帰る くる
phrases.translation: As for menma, [she] still hasn't returned / didn't come home yet.
phrases.notes: mada: still (don't mix it up with mata - again)

phrases.japanese: めんままだ髪長いのか
phrases.reading: めんま まだ かみ ながい の か
phrases.lemmaField: めんま まだ 髪 長い の か まだまだ
phrases.romaji: menma mada kami nagai no ka
phrases.translation: Is menma's hair still long?
phrases.notes:
mada: still (don't mix it up with mata - again)
kami: hair

phrases.reading: ちがう ちがう よ
phrases.lemmaField: 違う 違う よ
phrases.translation: Wrong, [this optinion / anwer is] wrong.
phrases.notes: chigau: to differ (from); to vary; to not match the correct (answer, etc.)

phrases.reading: ちがう だろ きりやま
phrases.lemmaField: 違う だ 桐山
phrases.translation: [I] guess kiriyama is wrong.
phrases.notes: chigau: to differ (from); to vary; to not match the correct (answer, etc.)

phrases.reading: ちがいます か
phrases.lemmaField: 違う か
phrases.translation: Is [this answer] wrong?
phrases.notes: chigau: to differ (from); to vary; to not match the correct (answer, etc.)

phrases.japanese: 違う違うただのバイトだよ
phrases.reading: ちがう ちがう ただ の ばいと だ よ
phrases.lemmaField: 違う 違う ただ の バイト だ よ
phrases.romaji: chigau chigau tada no baito da yo
phrases.translation: No, no, [it's] just an ordinary side job.
phrases.notes:
tada: ordinary, common
chigau: to differ (from); to vary; to not match the correct (answer, etc.)

phrases.japanese: 昔と全然違うんだけど
phrases.reading: むかし と ぜんぜん ちがう ん だ けど
phrases.lemmaField: 昔 と 全然 違う ん だ けど
phrases.romaji: mukashi to zenzen chigau n da kedo
phrases.translation: [Look at how the city has changed.] It's completely different from the olden days.
phrases.notes: Note that the "to" particle is used to indicate a comparison here. Whenever you're confused by some particle use, you might want to look at this list.

phrases.reading: あの とき の みょう な ひと
phrases.lemmaField: あの 時 の 妙 だ 人
phrases.romaji: ano toki no myou na hito
phrases.translation: [It's] the weird person from that time [before].
phrases.notes:
toki: time; hour; moment​ or also: occasion

Here, the speaker is meeting some strange person she met before.
phrases.source: Boku no Hero Academia S2 (ep 1-25 jp_en)

phrases.japanese: あのとき僕が言ってほしかったのは
phrases.reading: あの とき ぼく が いって ほしかった の は
phrases.lemmaField: あの とき 僕 が 言う ほしい の は
phrases.romaji: ano toki boku ga itte hoshikatta no ha
phrases.translation: At that time, what I wanted you to say was...
phrases.notes:
toki: time; hour; moment​ or also: occasion

Reminder: -te hoshii is used to express things that you want to have done, not things you want to do yourself.

phrases.japanese: 君はあのとき笑っていたから
phrases.reading: きみ は あの とき わらって いた から
phrases.lemmaField: 君 は あの とき 笑う いる から
phrases.romaji: kimi ha ano toki waratte ita kara
phrases.translation: [I thought it was funny] because you were laughing at that time.
phrases.notes: toki: time; hour; moment​ or also: occasion

phrases.reading: おとこ なら たたかう とき が くる
phrases.lemmaField: 男 だ 戦う 時 が くる
phrases.romaji: otoko nara tatakau toki ga kuru
phrases.translation: If [you are a] man, fighting-times are coming -> you will have to stand your ground.
phrases.notes: toki: time; hour; moment​ or also: occasion

phrases.japanese: あの時怖い夢を見ていて
phrases.reading: あの とき こわい ゆめ を みて いて
phrases.lemmaField: あの 時 怖い 夢 を 見る いる
phrases.romaji: ano toki kowai yume wo mite ite
phrases.translation: At that time [I] was seeing weird dreams and.... [didn't know what to do about it].
phrases.notes:
Reminder: The "and..." in the end is a consequence of the te-form.

toki: time; hour; moment​ or also: occasion

phrases.japanese: 初めて会った時のこと覚えてる
phrases.reading: はじめて あった とき の こと おぼえてる
phrases.lemmaField: 初めて 会う 時 の こと 覚える
phrases.romaji: hajimete atta toki no koto oboeteru
phrases.translation: Do [you] remember the time when [we] first met?

phrases.japanese: ケンカもあったしすごい楽しい時もあったし
phrases.reading: けんか も あった し すごい たのしい とき も あった し
phrases.lemmaField: ケンカ も ある し すごい 楽しい 時 も ある し
phrases.romaji: kenka mo atta shi sugoi tanoshii toki mo atta shi
phrases.translation: There were quarrels / disputes [among other things] and very enjoyable times.
phrases.notes: toki: time; hour; moment​ or also: occasion

phrases.reading: なぜ わたし に こえ を かける
phrases.lemmaField: なぜ 私 に 声 を かける
phrases.romaji: naze watashi ni koe wo kakeru
phrases.translation: Why do you talk to me?
phrases.notes:
koe: voice
koe wo kakeru: to greet; to call out (to); to start talking (to)

phrases.reading: い いま の おと なに だろう
phrases.lemmaField: いる 今 の 音 何 だ
phrases.romaji: i ima no oto nani darou
phrases.translation: The noise [we just heard], what is it?
phrases.notes: oto: sound; noise; report

phrases.japanese: わたしが声をかけました
phrases.reading: わたし が こえ を かけました
phrases.lemmaField: わたし が 声 を かける
phrases.translation: [And then] I started to talk [to him].
phrases.notes:
koe: voice
koe wo kakeru: to greet; to call out (to); to start talking (to)

phrases.reading: なに の おと です か それ
phrases.lemmaField: 何 の 音 です か それ
phrases.romaji: nani no oto desu ka sore
phrases.translation: What noise is this?

phrases.reading: はやく はいって くれ
phrases.lemmaField: 早い 入る くれる
phrases.translation: Come in / enter quickly (command form, rough / unfriendly!)
phrases.notes: hairu: to enter; to go into; to join

phrases.japanese: 部屋に入らせてもらうけどいい
phrases.reading: へや に はいらせて もらう けど いい
phrases.lemmaField: 部屋 に 入る もらう けど いい
phrases.romaji: heya ni hairasete morau kedo ii
phrases.translation: [It might be untidy] but I'd like to receive [you] letting me into the room. Good?
phrases.notes: hairu: to enter; to go into; to join

phrases.japanese: お前かわいい声してるよな
phrases.reading: おまえ かわいい こえ してる よ な
phrases.lemmaField: お前 かわいい 声 する よ な
phrases.romaji: omae kawaii koe shiteru yo na
phrases.translation: You are [talking in / making a] cute voice, aren't you.
phrases.source: Kokoro ga Sakebitagatterunda (Anthem of the Heart)

phrases.japanese: この家に入らないでくれ
phrases.reading: この いえ に はいらないで くれ
phrases.lemmaField: この 家 に 入る くれる
phrases.translation: Give me the favor of not entering this house!
phrases.notes: I'd say the speaker is talking to a youkai (type of ghost, the entire anime revolves around this), so a rough command might be appropriate: "kure" is the command form of "kureru". Even though you hear it often in anime, try not to get used to it too much. Remember what Tae Kim wrote: "This command form is quite rude so you should use it with caution (if at all)"

phrases.reading: どう した の その かお
phrases.lemmaField: どう する の その 顔
phrases.translation: Whats wrong? [Why are you making] this face?!
phrases.notes:
dou shita no: What's wrong? What happened?
kao: face

phrases.japanese: どこからか声が聞こえるぞ
phrases.reading: どこ から か こえ が きこえる ぞ
phrases.lemmaField: どこ から か 声 が 聞こえる ぞ
phrases.romaji: doko kara ka koe ga kikoeru zo
phrases.translation: From somewhere [I] can hear a voice?!
phrases.notes: Just in case you noticed: "doko kara ka" means "from somewhere". Instead, you could also use "doko ka kara". Don't worry about the difference.
phrases.source: JoJos Bizzare Adventure スターダストクルセイダース

phrases.japanese: まあそうかもしれないけどなあ
phrases.reading: まあ そう かもしれない けど なあ
phrases.lemmaField: まあ そう かもしれる けど なあ
phrases.translation: Well, maybe it's like this [like you said].
phrases.notes: maa - well...; I think...; it would seem... It's used when hesitating to express an opinion.

phrases.japanese: あの笑顔をまた見たい
phrases.reading: あの えがお を また みたい
phrases.lemmaField: あの 笑顔 を また 見る
phrases.translation: [I] would like to see this smile again.
phrases.notes: egao: smile

phrases.japanese: だっ大丈夫大丈夫敵じゃないぞ
phrases.reading: だっだいじょうぶ だいじょうぶ てき じゃない ぞ
phrases.lemmaField: だ 大丈夫 敵 じゃ ぞ
phrases.translation: It's ok, it's ok, [I] am not [your] enemy.
phrases.notes: teki: enemy

phrases.japanese: 変な返事だなまあいいけど
phrases.reading: へん な へんじ だ な まあ いい けど
phrases.lemmaField: 変 だ 返事 だ な まあ いい けど
phrases.romaji: hen na henji da na maa ii kedo
phrases.translation: [That's] a weird answer, isn't it? Well, but it's fine...
phrases.notes: maa - well...; I think...; it would seem... It's used when hesitating to express an opinion.

phrases.reading: しんぱい して いました
phrases.lemmaField: 心配 する いる
phrases.translation: [I] was worrying.
phrases.notes: shinpai: worry; concern

phrases.japanese: 敵を作ってしまうかもしれない
phrases.reading: てき を つくって しまう かもしれない
phrases.lemmaField: 敵 を 作る しまう かもしれる
phrases.translation: [We] might be making an enemy (unintentionally, by the things they are currently doing - whatever this might be, I haven't seen this anime).

phrases.japanese: 心配してくれてありがとう
phrases.reading: しんぱい して くれて ありがとう
phrases.lemmaField: 心配 する くれる ありがとう
phrases.translation: Thank you for giving [me] the favor of worrying [about me].

phrases.japanese: おかしいなあなたの顔見えない
phrases.reading: おかしい な あなた の かお みえない
phrases.lemmaField: おかしい な あなた の 顔 見える
phrases.romaji: okashii na anata no kao mienai
phrases.translation: Strange, isn't it! [I] can't see your face.

phrases.japanese: 俺みんなにも心配かけてるよな
phrases.reading: おれ みんな に も しんぱい かけてる よ な
phrases.lemmaField: 俺 みんな に も 心配 かける よ な
phrases.romaji: ore minna ni mo shinpai kaketeru yo na
phrases.translation: [I am not only causing trouble for you, but] I am also causing worries for the others.
phrases.notes: I already mentioned it on an earlier card: "kakeru" and "tsukeru" have many uses, just have a look at the dictionary. For these words, the dictionary often didn't help, but you'll get used to the words over time.

phrases.japanese: 心配することはないよ
phrases.reading: しんぱい する こと は ない よ
phrases.lemmaField: 心配 する こと は ない よ
phrases.romaji: shinpai suru koto ha nai yo
phrases.translation: [This] is not a worry-matter -> not a thing to worry about.

phrases.japanese: とにかくおいしいです
phrases.reading: とにかく おいしい です
phrases.lemmaField: とにかく おいしい です
phrases.translation: [This dish looks a bit weird....] anyway, it's tasty!
phrases.notes: tonikaku: anyhow; at any rate; anyway; somehow or other; generally speaking

phrases.japanese: とにかく調べてみるか
phrases.reading: とにかく しらべて みる か
phrases.lemmaField: とにかく 調べる みる か
phrases.translation: [Yes, I know it's difficult to get information on this topic] Anyhow, should [I] try to find out?
phrases.notes: tonikaku: anyhow; at any rate; anyway; somehow or other; generally speaking

phrases.japanese: 結局僕は何もできなかった
phrases.reading: けっきょく ぼく は なにも できなかった
phrases.lemmaField: 結局 僕 は 何も できる
phrases.translation: In the end I could not do anything.
phrases.notes: kekkyoku: after all; in the end; ultimately; eventually

phrases.japanese: 結局全然勉強できなかったの
phrases.reading: けっきょく ぜんぜん べんきょう できなかった の
phrases.lemmaField: 結局 全然 勉強 できる の
phrases.translation: [It was super loud in the library and I went home] because in the end I couldn't study.
phrases.notes: kekkyoku: after all; in the end; ultimately; eventually

phrases.reading: にほんご で いい よ
phrases.lemmaField: 日本語 だ いい よ
phrases.translation: It's ok [if you say it] in Japanese.
phrases.notes: nihongo: Japanese (language)

phrases.reading: えいご です
phrases.lemmaField: 英語 です
phrases.translation: It's English (e.g. the language some people close to them are speaking).
phrases.notes: eigo: English

phrases.japanese: 今日から君も僕の家族だ
phrases.reading: きょう から きみ も ぼく の かぞく だ
phrases.lemmaField: 今日 から 君 も 僕 の 家族 だ
phrases.romaji: kyou kara kimi mo boku no kazoku da
phrases.translation: From today you too are [part of my] family.
phrases.notes: kazoku: family

phrases.reading: はずかしい しゃしん
phrases.lemmaField: 恥ずかしい 写真
phrases.translation: [This is an] embarassing picture!
phrases.notes: shashin: picture

phrases.japanese: 家族は大事にしないとな
phrases.reading: かぞく は だいじ に しない と な
phrases.lemmaField: 家族 は 大事 に する と な
phrases.romaji: kazoku ha daiji ni shinai to na
phrases.translation: [You] must take good care of [your] family.
phrases.notes:
kazoku: family
daiji: important; serious; crucial
daiji ni suru: to take good care of

Reminder: "must do [something]" is expressed by:  [something] shinai to dame -> not doing [something] is bad. For "to", the "dame" may be omitted.

phrases.reading: おとな の たべもの だ
phrases.lemmaField: 大人 の 食べ物 だ
phrases.translation: [Yeah, I understand it's not tasty. This] is a dish / food for adults.
phrases.notes: otona: adult; grown-up

phrases.reading: こんな ところに すむ の か
phrases.lemmaField: こんな 所 住む の か
phrases.translation: [I have to] live in a place like this?
phrases.notes: sumu: to live (of humans); to reside; to inhabit

phrases.japanese: なんでお前が大河の写真を
phrases.reading: なんで おまえ が たいが の しゃしん を
phrases.lemmaField: なんで お前 が 大河 の 写真 を
phrases.romaji: nande omae ga taiga no shashin wo
phrases.translation: Why do you [have] a picture of taiga? (there's a "motsu no ka" missing in the end)

phrases.japanese: 僕には大人の人は分かりません
phrases.reading: ぼく に は おとな の ひと は わかりません
phrases.lemmaField: 僕 に は 大人 の 人 は 分かる
phrases.romaji: boku ni ha otona no hito ha wakarimasen
phrases.translation: As for me, [I] don't understand adults.
phrases.notes: otona no hito: adult

phrases.japanese: ‪大人になると‬あれできなくなるよね
phrases.reading: ‪ おとな に なる と ‬ あれ できなく なる よ ね
phrases.lemmaField: ‪ 大人 に なる と ‬ あれ できる なる よ ね
phrases.romaji: ‪ otona ni naru to ‬ are dekinaku naru yo ne
phrases.translation: When [you] become an adult, [you] can't do this anymore (literally: this becomes not-being-able-to-do).

phrases.japanese: １人でこんなところに住んでいるのだろうか
phrases.reading: ひとり で こんな ところ に すんで いる の だろう か
phrases.lemmaField: １人 で こんな ところ に 住む いる の だ か
phrases.romaji: hitori de konna tokoro ni sunde iru no darou ka
phrases.translation: [I] wonder if [he] lives alone in this place.

phrases.japanese: 私も大人になったしいっぱい勉強した
phrases.reading: わたし も おとな に なった し いっぱい べんきょう した
phrases.lemmaField: 私 も 大人 に なる し いっぱい 勉強 する
phrases.romaji: watashi mo otona ni natta shi ippai benkyou shita
phrases.translation: [This time I can do it!] I also became an adult [e.g. more mature among other things] and studied a lot!
phrases.source: The World God Only Knows S2 (jp eng)

phrases.japanese: 私には家族も友達もいる｡
phrases.reading: わたし に は かぞく も ともだち も いる ｡
phrases.lemmaField: 私 に は 家族 も 友達 も いる ｡
phrases.romaji: watashi ni ha kazoku mo tomodachi mo iru ｡
phrases.translation: [I am not alone]. I have both family and friends.
phrases.notes: xxx mo yyy mo means: both xxx and yyy.

phrases.japanese: こんなところに住みたいな
phrases.reading: こんな ところに すみたい な
phrases.lemmaField: こんな ところ 住む な
phrases.translation: [I] want to live in this place.

phrases.reading: しゃしん とる ん だ
phrases.lemmaField: 写真 撮る ん だ
phrases.translation: [Let's wait] because [he] takes a picture.
phrases.notes: shashin wo toru: to take a picture

phrases.japanese: それのどこがおかしいんだよ家族なんだ
phrases.reading: それ の どこ が おかしい ん だ よ かぞく なんだ
phrases.lemmaField: それ の どこ が おかしい ん だ よ 家族 なんだ
phrases.romaji: sore no doko ga okashii n da yo kazoku nanda
phrases.translation: Which [part] of [doing] thas is strange? [I did it for my] family!
phrases.notes:
The speaker did something for his family, which is considered strange by someone else here. He defends himself by saying this.

okashii: strange; odd; funny (don't mix this up with "okashi - sweets").

Remark: "sore no doko" literally means: "the "where" of that", which translates to "which part". It might take a while to digest this...

phrases.reading: しゃしん を とってる の か
phrases.lemmaField: 写真 を 撮る の か
phrases.translation: [Are you] taking a picture?

phrases.japanese: あっその前に写真撮りまーす
phrases.reading: あっその まえ に しゃしん とりま ー す
phrases.lemmaField: あっ 前 に 写真 撮りま ー する

phrases.japanese: またあとで来てくれないかな

phrases.japanese: きっとすてきなことだと思うの

phrases.japanese: きっと特別な力があるのよ

phrases.japanese: 今日はお空も泣いていますね
phrases.reading: きょう は お そら も ないて います ね
phrases.lemmaField: 今日 は お 空 も 泣く いる ね
phrases.romaji: kyou ha o sora mo naite imasu ne
phrases.translation: As for today, the sky is crying, too [maybe it's raining and something sad happened].

phrases.reading: ちがった よう だ
phrases.lemmaField: 違う よう だ ようです
phrases.translation: It appears [this] was wrong.
phrases.notes:
you: appearance, manner; It's a noun used to express simliarity, which often translates to "it appears that ..." or "it looks like...". Here's the dictionary definition.

Literally, this sentence would translate to something like: [this] is wrong-appearance. This way of expressing similarity, appearance and hearsay is very different from English, it takes a while to get used to this.

phrases.reading: ここ に なに の よう だ
phrases.lemmaField: ここ に 何 の 用 だ
phrases.romaji: koko ni nani no you da
phrases.translation: [There seem to be intruders here!] What business [do you have] here?!
phrases.notes:
you also means: business; task; errand

The "you" from the previous card meaning "appearance, manner" is usually written in kana: "よう", while this one is spelled in kanji: 用.

phrases.japanese: 用はないのただ名前を呼んでほしくて
phrases.reading: よう は ない の ただ なまえ を よんで ほしくて
phrases.lemmaField: 用 は ない の ただ 名前 を 呼ぶ ほしい
phrases.romaji: you ha nai no tada namae wo yonde hoshikute
phrases.translation: [This has] no purpose, [I] just wanted you to call my [first] name [the speaker has a crush on the listener and wants him to stop being so formal and use her first name].
phrases.notes:
you: use, purpose but also: business, task, errand

The "you" from the previous card meaning "appearance, manner" is usually written in kana: "よう", while this one is spelled in kanji: 用.

Updated in v14

you: appearance, manner; It's a noun used to express simliarity, which often translates to "it appears that ..." or "it looks like...". Here's the dictionary definition.

phrases.japanese: 昔のようにはならないだろう
phrases.reading: むかし の よう に は ならない だろう
phrases.lemmaField: 昔 の よう に は なる だ
phrases.romaji: mukashi no you ni ha naranai darou
phrases.translation: [I] guess [it] will not become like it was before.
phrases.notes:
mukashi no you: like before, literally: past-appearance.

It takes a while to get used to this "Japanese" way of expressing similarity or hearsay.

phrases.japanese: 犬のようにしてくれる
phrases.reading: いぬ の よう に して くれる
phrases.lemmaField: 犬 の よう に する くれる
phrases.romaji: inu no you ni shite kureru
phrases.translation: Can [you] do this for me like a [real] dog? [In this anime, the speaker often treats  the listener like a servant. She considers him her personal service dog].
phrases.notes:
inu no you: like a dog

It takes a while to get used to this "Japanese" way of expressing similarity or hearsay.

phrases.japanese: 大きくなったら私の髪もお母さんのようになる
phrases.reading: おおきく なったら わたし の かみ も おかあさん の よう に なる
phrases.lemmaField: 大きい なる 私 の 髪 も お母さん の よう に なる
phrases.romaji: ookiku nattara watashi no kami mo okaasan no you ni naru
phrases.translation: When I become big [grow up], will my hair become like my mother's?

phrases.japanese: 誰かいたような気がしたの
phrases.reading: だれ か いた よう な き が した の
phrases.lemmaField: 誰 か いる よう な 気 が する の ような
phrases.romaji: dare ka ita you na ki ga shita no
phrases.translation: [The place was empty. However, it was scary] because it felt like someone was there.
phrases.notes:
Very interesting sentence construction:
dareka ita - someone was there
dareka ita you - someone was there-appearance -> it appeared like someone was there
ki ga suru - to have a hunch / feeling of

Here, "you" is used as na-adjective to describe "ki - spirit, mood, feeling". So the speaker is suru-ing a someone-appeared-to-be-there feeling.

phrases.japanese: 何か忘れているような気がするが
phrases.reading: なにか わすれて いる よう な き が する が
phrases.lemmaField: 何か 忘れる いる よう な 気 が する が
phrases.romaji: nanika wasurete iru you na ki ga suru ga
phrases.translation: It feels like [I'm] forgetting something.
phrases.notes:
nanika wasurete iru - I am forgetting something
nanika wasurete iru you - It appears like I am forgetting something
ki ga suru - to have a hunch / feeling of

Again "you" as na-adjective to describe "ki - spirit, mood, feeling": The speaker is suru-ing an it-appears-I-am-forgetting-something feeling.

phrases.japanese: 似たような人を知ってるから
phrases.reading: にた よう な ひと を しってる から
phrases.lemmaField: 似る よう な 人 を 知る から
phrases.romaji: nita you na hito wo shitteru kara
phrases.translation: [I] know a person that appears to be similar / appears to look the same.
phrases.grammarNote: Ignore the "kara"
phrases.notes:
niru - to resemble; to look like; to be like; to be alike; to be similar

Without "you na", this would mean: I know someone who looked exactly the same as your dad. The "you na" adds some uncertainty: The person appears to look the same.

Remark: The verb before "you" does not have to be in past tense.

phrases.japanese: 謝るようなことじゃないんだ
phrases.reading: あやまる よう な こと じゃない ん だ
phrases.lemmaField: 謝る よう な こと じゃ ん だ

phrases.translation: [I don't apologize] because [this] doesn't appear to be an apologize-thing -> this doesn't appear to be something I should apologize for.
phrases.notes: I find some of these "you"-examples quite hard to translate to English...

phrases.japanese: 面白いような気がする

phrases.lemmaField: 面白い よう な 気 が する 面白そう

phrases.lemmaField: 仲間 は 私 にとって 家族 の よう な もの だ

phrases.translation: As for partner, to me [he] was a thing like family -> my partner was like family to me.
phrases.notes: nitotte: to; for; from the standpoint of; as far as ... is concerned​ (it's actually "ni totte", but I found it easier to learn it as one expression).

phrases.japanese: 前のようにみんなと一緒に

phrases.lemmaField: 前 の よう みんな と 一緒 に

phrases.grammarNote: Add an "tabetai - want to eat" in the end. The context is actually different, but it's the example that matters...

phrases.lemmaField: バカ みたい 恥ずかしい

phrases.grammarNote: Note the pause between mitai and hayzukashii
phrases.notes:
mitai: -like; sort of; similar to; resembling​. It's used in a similar way as "you/よう" to explain that something looks like something else. It's rather used in spoken Japanese and more casual than "you/よう".

Don't mix this up with "mitai - want to see".

phrases.japanese: よさそうだな高そうだけど
phrases.reading: よさそう だ な たかそう だ けど
phrases.lemmaField: よさそう だ な 高いそう だ けど
phrases.romaji: yosasou da na takasou da kedo
phrases.translation: [This] looks good! But it seems to be / looks expensive.
phrases.notes:
Remember the irregular conjugation of ii - good? It also applies here: ii is from yoi (which practically is not used - only for conjugating). So "isou" is wrong, instead use "yosasou".

-sou: appearing that; seeming that; looking like; having the appearance
This is just another example for expressing similarity/appearance. Don't worry about the difference to the others for now, just translate it like the others.

phrases.reading: げんき そう ね はい ぴか

phrases.notes:
-sou: appearing that; seeming that; looking like; having the appearance
This is just another example for expressing similarity/appearance. Don't worry about the difference to the others for now, just translate it like the others.

For na-adjectives, simply add "sou".

phrases.japanese: 悪くなさそうね良かった
phrases.reading: わるくなさそう ね よかった
phrases.lemmaField: 悪いそう ね 良い
phrases.translation: [He] seems to be not bad / at fault, good!
phrases.notes:
To express similarity/appearance for all negative words (except nouns), replace "nai" with "nasasou". This is rare!

For nouns, use "deshou" instead.

phrases.japanese: そんな幸せそうな顔しないで
phrases.reading: そんな しあわせそう な かお しないで
phrases.lemmaField: そんな 幸せそう だ 顔 する
phrases.translation: Don't make such a happy-looking face -> literally: don't make such an appears-to-be-happy face!
phrases.notes: Why is "sou" used here? I'd say that it is more polite to say "shiawasesou na kao - seems like your face looks happy" instead of "shiawase na kao - your face is happy". It's very similar to the use of "-tai": You don't know what the other person really is like.

phrases.japanese: ナルトは何でも食べそうだけど｡

phrases.lemmaField: ナルト は 何 でも 食べるそう だ けど ｡

phrases.notes: Why is "sou" used here? I'd say that it is more polite to say "nandemo tabesou - seems to eat everything", because you don't know if it's really true.

phrases.japanese: おこんな時間に起きてるなんて珍しい

phrases.reading: こまった らしい よ
phrases.lemmaField: 困る らしい よ あるらしい
phrases.translation: Seems like [they were] in trouble.
phrases.notes:
rashii: seeming ...; appearing ...​; -ish
Yet another word for expressing similarity/appearance/hearsay. The difference to the others is that "rashii" is less specific. E.g. using "-sou", you draw a conclusion from something specific: You look at a dish and say: oishisou - this specific one looks delicions. You could also say: oishii rashii - you somewhere heard that something about this dish is delicious. Again, don't worry and just translate it like the others.

phrases.notes:
rashii: seeming ...; appearing ...​; -ish
Yet another word for expressing similarity/appearance/hearsay. The difference to the others is that "rashii" is less specific. E.g. using "-sou", you draw a conclusion from something specific: You look at a dish and say: oishisou - this specific one looks delicions. You could also say: oishii rashii - you somewhere heard that something about this dish is delicious. Again, don't worry and just translate it like the others.

phrases.reading: せんせい っぽい

phrases.translation: [Don't act like this] it's kid-like [among other things].
phrases.notes: ppoi: slang expression for similarity (very casual).

phrases.japanese: 昨日俺に変って言ったじゃん
phrases.reading: きのう おれ に へん って いった じゃん
phrases.lemmaField: 昨日 俺 に 変 と 言う じゃん
phrases.romaji: kinou ore ni hen tte itta jan
phrases.translation: Yesterday, didn't [you] say "[you're] weird" to me? -> continues on next card.
phrases.notes: kinou: yesterday

phrases.japanese: でもお前のほうが変だよ
phrases.reading: でも おまえ の ほう が へん だ よ
phrases.lemmaField: でも お前 の ほう が 変 だ よ
phrases.romaji: demo omae no hou ga hen da yo
phrases.translation: [Yesterday, didn't [you] say "you're weird" to me?] But you are weirder!
phrases.notes:
hou: indicates one side of a comparison. When used as "xxx no hou ga yyy" this means: "The direction of xxx is more yyy than something clear from context". It may take a bit of practice to grasp this, but I'm sure you can do it!
In short: xxx no hou ga yyy: xxx is more yyy than something clear from context.

phrases.japanese: 白い服のほうがいいと思う

phrases.lemmaField: 白い 服 の ほう が いい と 思う
phrases.romaji: shiroi fuku no hou ga ii to omou
phrases.translation: White clothes are better I think.
phrases.notes: xxx no hou ga yyy: xxx is more yyy than something clear from context.

phrases.japanese: こっちのほうがかわいい

phrases.lemmaField: こっち の ほう が かわいい

phrases.notes: xxx no hou ga yyy: xxx is more yyy than something clear from context.

phrases.japanese: あれ私の方が早かったのかな

phrases.notes: xxx no hou ga yyy: xxx is more yyy than something clear from context.

phrases.reading: おれ の ほう が つよい

phrases.notes: xxx no hou ga yyy: xxx is more yyy than something clear from context.

phrases.japanese: お前のほうがずるいだろう
phrases.reading: おまえ の ほう が ずるい だろう
phrases.lemmaField: お前 の ほう が ずるい だ

phrases.notes: xxx no hou ga yyy: xxx is more yyy than something clear from context.

phrases.japanese: ああ家には帰った方がいい
phrases.reading: ああ いえ に は かえった ほう が いい
phrases.lemmaField: ああ 家 に は 帰る 方 が いい
phrases.romaji: aa ie ni ha kaetta hou ga ii
phrases.translation: Going home is better [than staying here].
phrases.notes:
xxx no hou ga yyy: xxx is more yyy than something clear from context.

Note the past tense "kaetta" here: Especially when making suggestions, past tense sounds more confident and certain. This does not mean that this happened in the past here.

phrases.reading: しらない ほう が しあわせ だ
phrases.lemmaField: 知る 方 が 幸せ だ
phrases.translation: Not knowing is happier -> I find "shiawase" always hard to translate, the sentence means that the speaker would be happier, if he didn't know something.
phrases.notes: xxx no hou ga yyy: xxx is more yyy than something clear from context.

phrases.reading: みない ほう が いい
phrases.lemmaField: 見る 方 が いい
phrases.translation: Not seeing is better -> It's better if [you] don't see [it].
phrases.notes: xxx no hou ga yyy: xxx is more yyy than something clear from context.

phrases.lemmaField: 勉強 する おく 方 が いい かもしれる
phrases.romaji: benkyou shite oita hou ga ii kamoshiren

phrases.notes:

Note the past tense "shite oita" here: Especially when making suggestions, past tense sounds more confident and certain. This does not mean that this happened in the past here.

phrases.japanese: 私も早く帰った方がいいと思います

phrases.notes:
xxx no hou ga yyy: xxx is more yyy than something clear from context.

phrases.japanese: あなたより僕のほうが強いので
phrases.reading: あなた より ぼく の ほう が つよい ので
phrases.lemmaField: あなた より 僕 の ほう が 強い ので
phrases.romaji: anata yori boku no hou ga tsuyoi node
phrases.translation: I am stronger than you (in an explanatory tone).
phrases.notes:
yori: sort of the opposite of "hou". It means "than" or "rather than", refers to the preceding word or clause and is often combined with "hou". The pattern or meaning is always something like this:

xxx yori, yyy no hou ga zzz: yyy is more zzz than xxx. 

Or as Tae Kim explains it: "hou" defines the direction the comparison is leaning toward while "yori" defines the side it’s leaning away from. You don't always have to use "hou".

phrases.notes:

yori: sort of the opposite of "hou". It means "than" or "rather than", refers to the preceding word or clause and is often combined with "hou". The pattern or meaning is always something like this:

xxx yori, yyy no hou ga zzz: yyy is more zzz than xxx. 

Or as Tae Kim explains it: "hou" defines the direction the comparison is leaning toward while "yori" defines the side it’s leaning away from. You don't always have to use "hou".

phrases.japanese: よく考えずにいったでしょ

phrases.notes: verb stem + zu: Indicates that this verb is not done while doing something else.

phrases.reading: さむい わけ だ
phrases.lemmaField: 寒い わけ だ
phrases.translation: [It's winter, ] this means / no wonder that [it] is cold!
phrases.notes:
wake (da): makes sense that / no wonder that / it means that 
The use of this word is a bit hard to describe: It's a noun used for making conlusions. Especially when used as "xxx wake da", it translates to what I wrote above, but it as usual depends a bit on the context.

phrases.japanese: 誰もついてこないというわけですな
phrases.reading: だれも ついて こない という わけ です な
phrases.lemmaField: 誰も つく くる という わけ です な

phrases.translation: [We were moving very fast, ] no wonder that noone followed us.
phrases.notes:
wake (da): makes sense that / no wonder that / it means that 
The use of this word is a bit hard to describe: It's a noun used for making conlusions. Especially when used as "xxx wake da", it translates to what I wrote above, but it as usual depends a bit on the context.

If the "to iu" here confuses you, just ignore it for now. It kind of emphasizes what comes before, but is a bit hard to explain. Have a look at maggie sensei's elaborate explanation in the references. She answers this in detail in this article and in the comments of this article.

phrases.japanese: 迷ってるわけですよ行こうか
phrases.reading: まよってる わけ です よ いこう か

phrases.translation: If you ignore the "ikou ka", this can mean: [We didn't bring a map] no wonder that [we're] lost.
phrases.notes:
However, "mayou" not only means "to be lost", but also "to hesitate; to be of two minds over; to be puzzled", which actually is the correct translation here:
[This is a very difficult decision] no wonder [I] am hesitating. Should we go?

wake (da): makes sense that / no wonder that / it means that 
The use of this word is a bit hard to describe: It's a noun used for making conlusions. Especially when used as "xxx wake da", it translates to what I wrote above, but it as usual depends a bit on the context.

phrases.japanese: できるわけがないだろそんなこと

It's not like [he] can do this.
There's no way he can do this.
phrases.notes:
wake ga nai / de ha nai / de ha arimasen, etc: it's not like that, there's no way that

wake ga nai / de ha nai / de ha arimasen, etc: it's not like that, there's no way that

phrases.japanese: 大事じゃないわけがないじゃないか
phrases.reading: だいじ じゃない わけ が ない じゃない か
phrases.lemmaField: 大事 じゃ わけ が ない じゃ か
phrases.romaji: daiji janai wake ga nai janai ka

Three negations in one sentence, omg ;D. Ignore the last "janai".

The speaker is telling his sister, that the father cares about her.

wake ga nai / de ha nai / de ha arimasen, etc: it's not like that, there's no way that

phrases.japanese: 忘れるワケにはいかない

phrases.japanese: 僕はまだ先生になったばかりだったけど
phrases.reading: ぼく は まだ せんせい に なった ばかり だった けど
phrases.lemmaField: 僕 は まだ 先生 に なる ばかり だ けど

phrases.notes: bakkari can also be used to express, that something has just happened (not only to express amounts as we learned before): Append it to the past tense of the verb.

phrases.japanese: 私も戻って来たばかりなので

phrases.japanese: 今来たばかりですけどね

phrases.notes: bakkari can also be used to express, that something has just happened (not only to express amounts as we learned before): Append it to the past tense of the verb.

phrases.notes: bakkari can also be used to express, that something has just happened (not only to express amounts as we learned before): Append it to the past tense of the verb.

phrases.japanese: 今教えたばかりだろうが
phrases.reading: いま おしえた ばかり だろう が

bakkari can also be used to express, that something has just happened (not only to express amounts as we learned before): Append it to the past tense of the verb.

phrases.japanese: まだ始まったばかりだぜ

phrases.notes: nagara: used to express concurrent actions: Append it to the stem of the first verb, this always means: to do something while doing something else.

phrases.notes: nagara: used to express concurrent actions: Append it to the stem of the first verb, this always means: to do something while doing something else.

phrases.japanese: 残念ながら冗談ではないんだよ
phrases.reading: ざんねん ながら じょうだん で は ない ん だ よ

phrases.romaji: zannen nagara joudan de ha nai n da yo
phrases.translation: While it's unfortunate, [this] is not a joke.
phrases.notes: nagara can also be attached to nouns. This describes that something is X and also Y. I'd just translate it like this, Tae Kim's explanation is a bit technical.

phrases.japanese: 泣いて泣いて泣きまくるだけじゃ
phrases.reading: ないて ないて なき まくる だけ じゃ
phrases.lemmaField: 泣く 泣く 泣く まくる だけ じゃ
phrases.romaji: naite naite naki makuru dake ja
phrases.translation: Crying, crying, [you are] crying [all the time / again and again].
phrases.notes:
The dictionary definition of "makuru" is funny:
makuru: to do over and over again; to do relentlessly; to do with reckless abandon to the activity

You can use this to express that an action is happening again and again by attaching this to the stem of the verb.

phrases.japanese: 何でも探しまくってよ

The dictionary definition of "makuru" is funny:
makuru: to do over and over again; to do relentlessly; to do with reckless abandon to the activity

You can use this to express that an action is happening again and again by attaching this to the stem of the verb.

phrases.japanese: 今のままだ何も変わらない

phrases.translation: In this state / condition, nothing changes.
phrases.notes:
mama: as it is; (current) state / condition; without changing ~.
mama is used to express something as it is, or to express a lack of change.

phrases.japanese: なんだ泥だらけじゃないかあ

phrases.japanese: 私はミツル君を信じるだからミツル君も私を信じて

phrases.translation: I believe [in] mitsuru-kun. Therefore, mitsuru-kun also believes [in] me...

phrases.japanese: 声出したら駄目だからね

phrases.japanese: どうすれば信じてくれる

If [I] do what/how/in which way, then will [you] give me the favor of believing [me]?

phrases.japanese: すみません大きいな声出して

phrases.notes:
dasu: to take out; to get out (this has many more meanings, but this one fits well most of the time)
koe wo dasu: to speak; to say: Rather in the sense of "saying something", or literally: to get out your voice

phrases.japanese: 私はそう信じています
phrases.reading: わたし は そう しんじて います
phrases.lemmaField: 私 は そう 信じる いる
phrases.translation: [This is] what [I am] believing.

phrases.japanese: また顔を出すんだろうな
phrases.reading: また かお を だす ん だろう な
phrases.lemmaField: また 顔 を 出す ん だ な
phrases.romaji: mata kao wo dasu n darou na
phrases.translation: [I] guess [he will] show up again.
phrases.notes:
dasu: to take out; to get out, to show (this has many more meanings, but this one fits well most of the time)
kao wo dasu: to show up, lit. to show your face

phrases.japanese: 今の俺の気持ちを感じてくれ
phrases.reading: いま の おれ の きもち を かんじて くれ
phrases.lemmaField: 今 の 俺 の 気持ち を 感じる くれる
phrases.romaji: ima no ore no kimochi wo kanjite kure
phrases.translation: Give [me] the favor of feeling my feelings.
phrases.notes: kanjiru: to feel; to sense; to experience

phrases.japanese: 私は本当に感じられるんだ
phrases.reading: わたし は ほんとうに かんじられる ん だ
phrases.lemmaField: 私 は 本当に 感じる ん だ
phrases.romaji: watashi ha hontouni kanjirareru n da
phrases.translation: [I] could really feel [it].
phrases.notes: kanjiru: to feel; to sense; to experience

phrases.japanese: 君も何かを感じただろうか
phrases.reading: きみ も なにか を かんじた だろう か
phrases.lemmaField: 君 も 何か を 感じる だ か
phrases.romaji: kimi mo nanika wo kanjita darou ka
phrases.translation: [I] wonder, if you could also feel something.
phrases.notes: kanjiru: to feel; to sense; to experience

phrases.reading: ひとつ だけ いえる こと が ある
phrases.lemmaField: １つ だけ 言える こと が ある
phrases.romaji: hitotsu dake ieru koto ga aru
phrases.translation: There's only one thing [I] can say.
phrases.notes: hitotsu: one (thing)

phrases.reading: いろいろ な こと が あった
phrases.lemmaField: 色々 だ こと が ある
phrases.translation: [When I returned home, ] all sorts of things had happened.
phrases.notes: iroiro: various; all sorts of; variety of

phrases.japanese: じゃあデパート探してデパート
phrases.reading: じゃあ でぱーと さがして でぱーと
phrases.lemmaField: じゃあ デパート 探す デパート
phrases.translation: Well, [let's] search for a department store. A department store!
phrases.notes: depa-to: department store; usually very large shopping malls where you can buy all kinds of things. I liked visiting them when I was in Japan, even though I don't like to go shopping very much. Have a look at the reference link if you're interested.

phrases.reading: たくさん ほん も よんだ
phrases.lemmaField: たくさん 本 も 読む
phrases.translation: [I am well prepared. I studied a lot and] even read a lot of books.
phrases.notes:
hon: book

"hon" also works with the store suffix we already had: honya - book store.

phrases.japanese: いろんなことがあったな
phrases.reading: いろんな こと が あった な
phrases.lemmaField: いろんな こと が ある な 色んな
phrases.translation: [When I returned home, ] all sorts of things had happened.
phrases.notes: ironna: slangy version of "iroiro na": various; all sorts of; variety of

phrases.japanese: １人でいる時間がこれほどまでに長く感じるとは
phrases.reading: ひとり で いる じかん が これ ほど まで に ながく かんじる と は
phrases.lemmaField: １人 で いる 時間 が これ ほど まで に 長い 感じる と は
phrases.romaji: hitori de iru jikan ga kore hodo made ni nagaku kanjiru to ha
phrases.translation: Being alone-time feels long to this extent -> The time when being alone passes slowly / feels long.
phrases.grammarNote: Ignore the "to ha" in the end for now.
phrases.notes:
hitori de iru: to be alone (used as clause for "jikan - time")
kore hodo made: to this extend
nagaku kanjiru: to feel long

to ha: Ignore it for now, it's used to quote someone (from "to iu no ha") / to indicate the topic and express the speaker’s surprise, see reference link for more information.

phrases.reading: みぎ みて ひだり みて
phrases.lemmaField: 右 見る 左 見る
phrases.translation: Look right, look left [that's what you do before crossing the road].
phrases.grammarNote: Look where they are standing.
phrases.notes: migi: right

phrases.reading: かお を だして ください
phrases.lemmaField: 顔 を 出す くださる
phrases.translation: Please come by / show up. -> Literally, the translation is something like "Please bring up / show your face".
phrases.notes:
dasu: to take out; to get out (this has many more meanings, but this one fits well most of the time)
kao wo dasu: to turn up; to make an appearance

phrases.reading: あの おんな が あぶない
phrases.lemmaField: あの 女 が 危ない
phrases.translation: This woman is dangerous:
phrases.notes: onna: female; woman; female sex​

phrases.japanese: それは私のお父さんの言葉
phrases.reading: それ は わたし の おとうさん の ことば
phrases.lemmaField: それ は 私 の お父さん の 言葉
phrases.romaji: sore ha watashi no otousan no kotoba
phrases.translation: As for that, those are my father's words (i.e. my father's way of speaking or: my father's opinion).
phrases.notes: kotoba: word, phrase; but also: language / way of speaking

phrases.reading: かみ の ながい おんな の ひと が
phrases.lemmaField: 髪 の 長い 女 の 人 が
phrases.romaji: kami no nagai onna no hito ga
phrases.translation: [It was the] woman with the long hair!
phrases.grammarNote: Ignore the "ga" in the end.

phrases.japanese: ああお前とキスした女か
phrases.reading: ああ おまえ と きす した おんな か
phrases.lemmaField: ああ お前 と キス する 女 か
phrases.romaji: aa omae to kisu shita onna ka
phrases.translation: Ah, [is this] the woman you kissed? lit. the woman that kissed with you?

phrases.japanese: いいよもう子供じゃないんだから
phrases.reading: いい よ もう こども じゃない ん だ から
phrases.lemmaField: いい よ もう 子供 じゃ ん だ から
phrases.romaji: ii yo mou kodomo janai n da kara
phrases.translation: It's ok [you can tell me] - because I'm not a kid [anymore].
phrases.notes: kodomo: child, kid

phrases.japanese: 図書館の本じゃないよ
phrases.reading: としょかん の ほん じゃない よ
phrases.lemmaField: 図書館 の 本 じゃ よ
phrases.translation: [This] is not a book from the library.
phrases.notes:
hon: book

"hon" also works with the store suffix we already had: honya - book store.
phrases.source: The World God Only Knows S1 (jp eng)

phrases.japanese: この町に女がいないこと知らなかった
phrases.reading: この まち に おんな が いない こと しらなかった
phrases.lemmaField: この 町 に 女 が いる こと 知る
phrases.romaji: kono machi ni onna ga inai koto shiranakatta
phrases.translation: [You] didn't know that there are no women in this town?

phrases.reading: かんぱい
phrases.lemmaField: 乾杯
phrases.translation: Cheers (the Japanese way to raise your glass).

phrases.reading: さあ はじめよう か
phrases.lemmaField: さあ 始める か
phrases.translation: Well, shall we start?
phrases.notes: hajimeru: to start; to begin; to commence

phrases.japanese: 右から何か来てるみたいだし
phrases.reading: みぎ から なに か きてる みたい だ し
phrases.lemmaField: 右 から 何 か 来る みたい だ し
phrases.romaji: migi kara nani ka kiteru mitai da shi
phrases.translation: Looks like something is coming from the right...
phrases.notes: migi: right

phrases.japanese: さっきから呼んでるのに全然返事してくれないです
phrases.reading: さっき から よんでる のに ぜんぜん へんじ して くれない です
phrases.lemmaField: さっき から 呼ぶ のに 全然 返事 する くれる です
phrases.romaji: sakki kara yonderu noni zenzen henji shite kurenai desu
phrases.translation: [I] have been calling out [to you] since a short while ago, but I didn't get an aswer at all. [B: Sorry, I was thinking about work].
phrases.notes:
sakki: a short while ago; a moment ago; just now; some time ago
Remark: yobu is not used for expressing to call someone on the phone, see ref. Here, the speakers are sitting on a table together.

phrases.reading: とても あつい なつ の
phrases.lemmaField: とても 暑い 夏 の とっても とてもとても
phrases.translation: [I don't like it here], because the summer is very hot.
phrases.notes: natsu: summer

phrases.japanese: 今私が聞きたいのはそんな言葉じゃない｡
phrases.reading: いま わたし が ききたい の は そんな ことば じゃない ｡
phrases.lemmaField: 今 私 が 聞く の は そんな 言葉 じゃ ｡ 詞
phrases.romaji: ima watashi ga kikitai no ha sonna kotoba janai ｡
phrases.translation: As for what I want to hear right now: It's not those words (or less literal: that's not what I want to hear right now).
phrases.notes: kotoba: word, phrase
phrases.source: Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dreaming Girl (Eng + Jp)

phrases.japanese: 女の子の気持ちなんて全然分かってない
phrases.reading: おんなのこ の きもち なんて ぜんぜん わかってない
phrases.lemmaField: 女の子 の 気持ち なんて 全然 分かる
phrases.romaji: onnanoko no kimochi nante zenzen wakattenai
phrases.translation: [You're] totally not understanding a girl's feelings!
phrases.notes:
onna no ko: young woman, girl

Note that parsing written Japanese is a bit inconsistent here, "onnanoko" is spelled together, while "onna no hito" had whitespaces on a previous card. It's quite some effort to correct this everywhere, so I just leave it as it is for now. Remember: Japanese has no whitespaces anyway. If spelled with kanji, this is much easier to read though: 女の子.

phrases.japanese: 日本語すごい上手ですね
phrases.reading: にほんご すごい じょうず です ね
phrases.lemmaField: 日本語 すごい 上手 です ね
phrases.translation: [Your] Japanese is super skillful -> something you will hear when you say a little more than "konnichiha" to a Japanese person ;).
phrases.notes: jouzu: skillful; skilled; proficient; good (at)

phrases.japanese: 子供じゃないかうまそう
phrases.reading: こども じゃない か うまそう
phrases.lemmaField: 子供 じゃ か うまいそう
phrases.translation: Isn't this a kid [over there]? Looks tasty! (seems like they want to eat it, I haven't seen this anime).
phrases.notes: kodomo: child, kid

phrases.japanese: さっきよりはよくなりましたよね
phrases.reading: さっき より は よく なりました よ ね
phrases.lemmaField: さっき より は よく なる よ ね
phrases.romaji: sakki yori ha yoku narimashita yo ne
phrases.translation: [Your skills] became better than a while ago.
phrases.notes:
sakki: a short while ago; a moment ago; just now; some time ago

Remark: The "ha" on this card has a slightly different use than what we learned before: It is used for contrasting what comes before with what comes after. In this case, it contrasts the past (sakki yori) and the present (rest of the sentence) and and puts a certain emphasis on "sakki yori". Most important: It does not make much of a difference in nuance, if it is there or not. See refs for details.

Remark 2: Actually, I am not sure if the contrasting use and the topic marking use are constructions made up by western grammar scholars, but this is just my opinion ;).

phrases.japanese: じゃあそろそろ切るね
phrases.reading: じゃあ そろそろ きる ね
phrases.lemmaField: じゃあ そろそろ 切る ね
phrases.translation: [I have to] hang up soon (i.e. to stop talking on the phone)
phrases.notes: kiru: to cut (paper, hair, vegetables), but also (like in this example): to hang up the phone

phrases.japanese: はーい授業を始めますよー
phrases.reading: はーい じゅぎょう を はじめます よー
phrases.lemmaField: はーい 授業 を 始める よー
phrases.translation: OK [everyone], class [is about to] start --> e.g. the teacher is asking the students to get to their seats.
phrases.notes:
hajimeru: to start; to begin; to commence

Remark: the "haaaai" in the beginning is often used to get the attention of someone.

phrases.japanese: こんなところに女の子がいるなんて
phrases.reading: こんな ところに おんなのこ が いる なんて
phrases.lemmaField: こんな ところ 女の子 が いる なんて
phrases.romaji: konna tokoroni onnanoko ga iru nante
phrases.translation: [It's strange,] a girl being at a place like this.

phrases.reading: ふゆ が たのしみ だ な
phrases.lemmaField: 冬 が 楽しみ だ な お楽しみ
phrases.translation: [I am] looking forward to winter.
phrases.notes: fuyu: winter

phrases.japanese: レゴシこの夏はどうだったのよ
phrases.reading: れごし この なつ は どう だった の よ
phrases.lemmaField: レゴシ この 夏 は どう だ の よ だったん
phrases.romaji: regoshi kono natsu ha dou datta no yo
phrases.translation: regoshi, as for this summer [you told us about], how was it?
phrases.notes: natsu: summer

phrases.japanese: でもね私たちにはお金が必要なんだ
phrases.reading: でも ね わたしたち に は おかね が ひつよう なんだ
phrases.lemmaField: でも ね 私たち に は お金 が 必要 なんだ
phrases.romaji: demo ne watashitachi ni ha okane ga hitsuyou nanda
phrases.translation: [I know it's not nice] but we need money!
phrases.grammarNote: Listen, the speaker is loading a gun...
phrases.notes:
hitsuyou: necessary; needed; essential; indispensable

This is another interesting example of different word types: In Japanese, it's a noun, while you would rather use a verb (need) in English.

phrases.japanese: その後どうなったかは誰も知らねえ
phrases.reading: そのご どう なった か は だれ も しらねえ
phrases.lemmaField: その後 どう なる か は 誰 も 知る
phrases.romaji: sonogo dou natta ka ha dare mo shiranee
phrases.translation: [What] happened afterwards, noone knows.
phrases.notes: sonogo: after that; afterwards (sometimes also pronounced "sonoato").

phrases.japanese: もっと上手になりたい
phrases.reading: もっと じょうず に なりたい
phrases.lemmaField: もっと 上手 に なる
phrases.translation: [I] want to become better [at this].
phrases.notes: jouzu: skillful; skilled; proficient; good (at)

phrases.japanese: でもやっぱり人の血は必要
phrases.reading: でも やっぱり ひと の ち は ひつよう
phrases.lemmaField: でも やっぱり 人 の 血 は 必要
phrases.romaji: demo yappari hito no chi ha hitsuyou
phrases.translation: But as expected, human blood is a requirement -> we need human blood [to complete this / to heal him...]
phrases.notes: yappari. as expected; sure enough; after all (is said and done); in the end

phrases.reading: ね かみ すこし きったら
phrases.lemmaField: ね 髪 少し 切る
phrases.translation: How about cutting [your] hair a bit? Literally: what if you cut your hair a bit (due to conditional form "kittara").
phrases.notes: kiru: to cut (paper, hair, vegetables), but also: to hang up the phone

phrases.japanese: もっとお金が必要になるよ
phrases.reading: もっと おかね が ひつよう に なる よ
phrases.lemmaField: もっと お金 が 必要 に なる よ
phrases.romaji: motto okane ga hitsuyou ni naru yo
phrases.translation: [We] will need more money [to finish this].

phrases.japanese: 二人はあのシガンシナ区の出身だよね
phrases.reading: ふたり は あの しがんしなく の しゅっしん だ よ ね
phrases.lemmaField: 二人 は あの シガンシナ区 の 出身 だ よ ね
phrases.romaji: futari ha ano shiganshinaku no shusshin da yo ne
phrases.translation: As for you two, [you are] from shinganshinaku, aren't you?
phrases.notes:
shusshin: one's origin (e.g. city, country, parentage, school)
Remark: I found names quite hard to understand...

phrases.reading: ここ の ふゆ は いい な
phrases.lemmaField: ここ の 冬 は いい な
phrases.romaji: koko no fuyu ha ii na
phrases.translation: The winter here is great, isn't it?
phrases.notes: fuyu: winter

phrases.reading: みず と お といれ は した よ
phrases.lemmaField: 水 と お トイレ は 下 よ
phrases.romaji: mizu to o toire ha shita yo
phrases.translation: Water and the toilet are downstairs -> the girl is renting a room in an old house. She doesn't have water and a toilet on this floor.
phrases.notes: shita: below; down; under
phrases.source: Kikis delivery service (魔女の宅急便)

phrases.japanese: さっきから何を気にしてるんだよ
phrases.reading: さっき から なに を き に してる ん だ よ
phrases.lemmaField: さっき から 何 を 気 に する ん だ よ
phrases.romaji: sakki kara nani wo ki ni shiteru n da yo
phrases.translation: What do you mind since recently? -> What is bothering you since a while ago?
phrases.grammarNote: Ignore the "n da yo" in the end.
phrases.notes:
ki ni suru: to mind (negative nuance); to care about

I found it hard to distinguish all these phrases with "ki".

phrases.reading: そのあと の じょうほう は なし
phrases.lemmaField: その後 の 情報 は ない
phrases.translation: As for after that, there's no information -> They are talking about a mysterious girl, but only know about her up so some point in time.
phrases.notes: sonoato: after that; afterwards (sometimes also pronounced "sonogo").

phrases.japanese: 黒いニャンコってかわいいな
phrases.reading: くろい にゃんこ って かわいい な
phrases.lemmaField: 黒い ニャンコ って かわいい な
phrases.translation: As for black cats, [they] are cute.
phrases.notes:
kuroi: black, dark
nyanko: kitty-cat (children's language). This is an important word in this anime, more on this later ;)

phrases.japanese: 別にお金をかける必要はないの
phrases.reading: べつ に おかね を かける ひつよう は ない の
phrases.lemmaField: 別 に お金 を かける 必要 は ない の にかけて
phrases.romaji: betsu ni okane wo kakeru hitsuyou ha nai no
phrases.translation: There's no need to spend money.
phrases.notes:
betsuni: (not) particularly; (not) especially; (not) specially
okane wo kakeru: to spend money

phrases.japanese: いいえそれは違います｡
phrases.reading: いいえ それ は ちがいます ｡
phrases.lemmaField: いいえ それ は 違う ｡
phrases.translation: No, as for that, [it's] wrong.
phrases.notes: iie: no -> make sure to read the article I linked as reference

phrases.reading: しゅっしん どこ です か
phrases.lemmaField: 出身 どこ です か
phrases.translation: As for [your origin], where is it? -> Where are you from?
phrases.notes: shusshin: one's origin (e.g. city, country, parentage, school)
phrases.source: Terrace House- Boys & Girls in the City

phrases.reading: まど を あけた の は だれ だ ?
phrases.lemmaField: 窓 を 開ける の は 誰 だ ?
phrases.romaji: mado wo aketa no ha dare da ?
phrases.translation: As for opened the window: Who is it? -> Who opened the window?
phrases.notes: mado: window

phrases.japanese: でもどうして人を傷つける必要があるんだろう
phrases.reading: でも どうして ひと を きずつける ひつよう が ある ん だろう
phrases.lemmaField: でも どうして 人 を 傷つける 必要 が ある ん だ
phrases.romaji: demo doushite hito wo kizutsukeru hitsuyou ga aru n darou
phrases.translation: But why is it necessary to wound / injure people?

phrases.japanese: それでみんなで結婚おめでとうって言いましょう
phrases.reading: それで みんな で けっこん おめでとう って いいましょう
phrases.lemmaField: それで みんな で 結婚 おめでとう って 言う
phrases.romaji: sorede minna de kekkon omedetou tte iimashou
phrases.translation: And now, let's say congratulations to [your] wedding with everybody!
phrases.notes:
kekkon: marriage (this ranks surprisingly high on my frequency lists)
sorede: so; therefore; and; (and) then, well

phrases.japanese: タケシじゃあその下の写真は
phrases.reading: たけし じゃあ その した の しゃしん は
phrases.lemmaField: タケシ じゃあ その 下 の 写真 は
phrases.romaji: takeshi jaa sono shita no shashin ha
phrases.translation: Ok, and what about the picture below [the one you just explained? They are looking at a larger gallery of pictures on the wall].
phrases.notes: shita: below; down; under

phrases.japanese: 全然感じが違いますよ
phrases.reading: ぜんぜん かんじ が ちがいます よ
phrases.lemmaField: 全然 感じ が 違う よ
phrases.translation: The feeling / impression [when drinking ordinary grape juice and freshly pressed juice] is completely different (they are really talking about juice here :D).
phrases.notes:
kanji: feeling; sense; impression
The word "kanji" is not only a Chinese character, but it also has this completely different meaning. I often found this quite hard to translate.

phrases.japanese: お前は兄弟と離れてはいかん
phrases.reading: おまえ は きょうだい と はなれて は いかん
phrases.lemmaField: お前 は 兄弟 と 離れる は いく
phrases.romaji: omae ha kyoudai to hanarete ha ikan
phrases.translation: As for you, [you] must not be separated from your siblings.
phrases.notes:
kyoudai: sibling(s), also: brothers
Reminder: "-te ha ikanai" means "must not"

phrases.japanese: 大丈夫大丈夫まだ黒くない
phrases.reading: だいじょうぶ だいじょうぶ まだ くろくない
phrases.lemmaField: 大丈夫 大丈夫 まだ 黒い
phrases.translation:
It's ok, it's ok, it's not black yet (they're talking about a silver spear. When it turns dark, the speaker will die - for whatever reason).
This sentence can also mean: It's not dark (outside) yet, i.e. the sun is still shining a bit.
phrases.notes: kuroi: black, dark

phrases.japanese: いいえ違うあなたは誰なの
phrases.reading: いいえ ちがう あなた は だれ な の
phrases.lemmaField: いいえ 違う あなた は 誰 だ の いえ いえいえ
phrases.romaji: iie chigau anata ha dare na no
phrases.translation: [You are Elizabeth...wait] no, wrong. Who are you?
phrases.notes: iie: no -> make sure to read the article I linked as reference

phrases.japanese: 窓から何かが入ってきて
phrases.reading: まど から なに か が はいって きて
phrases.lemmaField: 窓 から 何 か が 入る くる
phrases.romaji: mado kara nani ka ga haitte kite
phrases.translation: Something entered through the window and... [took pikachu]. Note that the past tense in this example comes from the second part of the sentence, which is missing here. This sentence is linked to the second one using the -te form.
phrases.notes:
mado: window
Reminder: -te iku and -te kuru direct the preceding verb (hairu - to enter) into a direction. kuru means, that the entering happens towards the speaker into the room.

phrases.japanese: まさかこんなことになるなんて
phrases.reading: まさか こんな こと に なる なんて
phrases.lemmaField: まさか こんな こと に なる なんて
phrases.romaji: masaka konna koto ni naru nante
phrases.translation: By no means [I expected] something like this [to happen]...
phrases.notes:
"masaka" is not always easy to translate directly. It is very common though and usually means, that something is unbelievable and not likely to be true. 
The official dictionary definition is: by no means; never!; well, I never!; you don't say!; certainly (not)

phrases.japanese: 私も結婚する前はそんなだったなあ
phrases.reading: わたし も けっこん する まえ は そんな だった なあ
phrases.lemmaField: 私 も 結婚 する 前 は そんな だ なあ なぁ
phrases.romaji: watashi mo kekkon suru mae ha sonna datta naa
phrases.translation: I also was like that before [I] got married.
phrases.notes: kekkon: marriage (this ranks surprisingly high on my frequency lists)

phrases.japanese: お前さあ学校でいっつも１人で本読んでるよな
phrases.reading: おまえ さあ がっこう で いっつも ひとり で ほん よんでる よ な
phrases.lemmaField: お前 さあ 学校 で いっつも １人 で 本 読む よ な 本屋
phrases.romaji: omae saa gakkou de ittsumo hitori de hon yonderu yo na
phrases.translation: You, at school [you] always read books alone, don't you.
phrases.notes:
hon: book

"hon" also works with the store suffix we already had: honya - book store.

phrases.japanese: 越智黒崎家の兄弟ケンカならあっちでやれ
phrases.reading: おち くろさきか の きょうだい けんか なら あっち で やれ
phrases.lemmaField: 越智 黒崎家 の 兄弟 ケンカ だ あっち で やる
phrases.romaji: ochi kurosakika no kyoudai kenka nara acchi de yare
phrases.translation: kurosakika brothers, if [you want to] fight, then [go] over there [out of the room].
phrases.notes: kyoudai: sibling(s), also: brothers

phrases.japanese: 茂田の右をよく見ておけ
phrases.reading: しげた の みぎ を よく みて おけ
phrases.lemmaField: 茂田 の 右 を よく 見る おく
phrases.romaji: shigeta no migi wo yoku mite oke
phrases.translation: Keep your eyes on shigeta's right, or more literal: Watch shigeta's right well.
phrases.notes: migi: right

phrases.reading: ことば に き を つけろ
phrases.lemmaField: 言葉 に 気 を つける
phrases.translation: Watch your tone (lit: pay attention to your words).
phrases.notes: kotoba: word, phrase; but also: language / way of speaking
phrases.source: The Disastrous Life of Saiki K. (Eng + Jp)

phrases.japanese: いつまでも子供のままと思わないでください
phrases.reading: いつ まで も こども の まま と おもわないで ください
phrases.lemmaField: いつ まで も 子供 の まま と 思う くださる
phrases.romaji: itsu made mo kodomo no mama to omowanaide kudasai
phrases.translation: Please don't think of me as a kid forever.
phrases.notes:
kodomo: child, kid
itsu made mo: forever, this is often taught as one word or phrase (itsumademo). Literally, it means something like "until even when".
Reminder 1: "to omou" is used to "quote" and talk about the previous phrase in the sense: to think. It's related to "to iu".
Reminder 2: mama is a noun and refers to a state. xxx no mama usually translates to "as xxx".
phrases.source: Daily Lives of High School Boys (Eng + Jp)

phrases.japanese: 俺がギター始めた時何やってたか覚えてる
phrases.reading: おれ が ぎたー はじめた とき なに やってた か おぼえてる
phrases.lemmaField: 俺 が ギター 始める 時 何 やる か 覚える
phrases.romaji: ore ga gita- hajimeta toki nani yatteta ka oboeteru
phrases.translation: At the time when I started [to play] the guitar, [do you] remember what [I] did [physical action]? -> e.g. what he did to improve, playing an instrument is hard, after all.
phrases.notes: hajimeru: to start; to begin; to commence

phrases.japanese: それ返すためにわざわざ来たの
phrases.reading: それ かえす ために わざわざ きた の
phrases.lemmaField: それ 返す ため わざわざ 来る の
phrases.romaji: sore kaesu tameni wazawaza kita no
phrases.translation: [You] explicitly came here for returning that?
phrases.notes:
tame ni: for; for the sake of; in order to
In some resources, this is often covered as topic of its own, but not found in Tae Kim's guide. Probably, because it is just the common use case of "ni" as Tae Kim explained it: ni marks the preceding word as target of a verb or clause. In this case, the preceding word is "tame - sake, purpose".

phrases.japanese: 夏になると町は怖いほど静かになる
phrases.reading: なつ に なる と まち は こわい ほど しずか に なる
phrases.lemmaField: 夏 に なる と 町 は 怖い ほど 静か に なる
phrases.romaji: natsu ni naru to machi ha kowai hodo shizuka ni naru
phrases.translation: When [it] becomes summer, the city becomes quiet to a scary degree.
phrases.notes: natsu: summer

phrases.japanese: お父さんお料理上手だからおいしいですよ
phrases.reading: おとうさん お りょうり じょうず だ から おいしい です よ
phrases.lemmaField: お父さん お 料理 上手 だ から おいしい です よ
phrases.romaji: otousan o ryouri jouzu da kara oishii desu yo
phrases.translation: [Your] father is good at food (=at cooking) so [eating at your place will be] tasty.
phrases.notes: jouzu: skillful; skilled; proficient; good (at)

phrases.japanese: 泳ぐこと嫌いになってしまいましたか
phrases.reading: およぐ こと きらい に なって しまいました か
phrases.lemmaField: 泳ぐ こと 嫌い に なる しまう か
phrases.romaji: oyogu koto kirai ni natte shimaimashita ka
phrases.translation: [After this incident] did swimming thing become disliked? -> Do you hate swimming now?
phrases.notes:
kirai: disliked; hated; disagreeable
Reminder: -te shimau describes unintended actions, often with bad outcome.

phrases.japanese: んまさか自分で切るの
phrases.reading: ん まさか じぶん で きる の
phrases.lemmaField: ん まさか 自分 で 切る の
phrases.romaji: n masaka jibun de kiru no
phrases.translation: Huh? No way, you cut [your hair] yourself?!
phrases.notes: kiru: to cut (paper, hair, vegetables), but also (like in this example): to hang up the phone

phrases.japanese: 寒さに強いと冬でも風邪をひかない
phrases.reading: さむさ に つよい と ふゆ で も かぜ を ひかない
phrases.lemmaField: 寒い に 強い と 冬 で も 風邪 を ひく 風
phrases.romaji: samusa ni tsuyoi to fuyu de mo kaze wo hikanai
phrases.translation: If [you] are strong against coldness, [you will] not catch a cold even though [it is] winter.
phrases.notes:
fuyu: winter
kaze wo hiku: to catch a cold

phrases.japanese: これじゃ走るのは無理だな
phrases.reading: これ じゃ はしる の は むり だ な
phrases.lemmaField: これ じゃ 走る の は 無理 だ な
phrases.romaji: kore ja hashiru no ha muri da na
phrases.translation: As for running, [this is] impossible [now, looks like the girl is injured]
phrases.notes: hashiru: to run

phrases.japanese: じゃあその後はどうするんだ
phrases.reading: じゃあ そのあと は どう する ん だ
phrases.lemmaField: じゃあ その後 は どう する ん だ んで
phrases.romaji: jaa sonoato ha dou suru n da
phrases.translation: As for afterwards, what [will] you do? -> well, and what will you do afterwards?
phrases.notes: sonoato: after that; afterwards

phrases.japanese: 二人はどこの出身なの
phrases.reading: ふたり は どこ の しゅっしん な の
phrases.lemmaField: 二人 は どこ の 出身 だ の
phrases.romaji: futari ha doko no shusshin na no
phrases.translation: As for you two, where are you from?
phrases.notes: shusshin: one's origin (e.g. city, country, parentage, school)

phrases.japanese: 食うためじゃなく殺すために殺したんだよ
phrases.reading: くう ため じゃなく ころす ために ころした ん だ よ
phrases.lemmaField: 食う ため じゃ 殺す ため 殺す ん だ よ いたん
phrases.romaji: kuu tame janaku korosu tameni koroshita n da yo
phrases.translation: Not [for] eat purpose [I killed], for kill purpose [I] killed.
phrases.notes:
tame ni: for; for the sake of; in order to
In some resources, this is often covered as topic of its own, but not found in Tae Kim's guide. Probably, because it is just the common use case of "ni" as Tae Kim explained it: ni marks the preceding word as target of a verb or clause. In this case, the preceding word is "tame - sake, purpose".

phrases.reading: ぼく も うたう の は すき だ
phrases.lemmaField: 僕 も 歌う の は 好き だ すき
phrases.romaji: boku mo utau no ha suki da
phrases.translation: I also like to sing.
phrases.notes: utau: to sing

phrases.japanese: そんなことを言う人大嫌いです
phrases.reading: そんな こと を いう ひと だいきらい です
phrases.lemmaField: そんな こと を 言う 人 大嫌い です
phrases.romaji: sonna koto wo iu hito daikirai desu
phrases.translation: [I] hate saying-such-thing people -> I hate people who say such things.
phrases.notes: daikirai: strong dislike, hating

phrases.japanese: じゃ下の名前教えてください
phrases.reading: じゃ した の なまえ おしえて ください
phrases.lemmaField: じゃ 下 の 名前 教える くださる
phrases.romaji: ja shita no namae oshiete kudasai
phrases.translation: Please tell me [your] given name.
phrases.notes:
Remark: In Japanese, you usually address people with their last name. When writing down names, the last name is written first. Moreover, Japanese is traditionally written from top to bottom, so the given name is below the last name. That's why given name literally is "bottom name" in Japanese, have a look at the reference.

shita: below; down; under

phrases.japanese: なんで一人で掃除してるんだ俺
phrases.reading: なんで ひとり で そうじ してる ん だ おれ
phrases.lemmaField: なんで 一人 で 掃除 する ん だ 俺
phrases.romaji: nande hitori de souji shiteru n da ore
phrases.translation: Why am I cleaning up alone? -> This guy loves to clean and to do housework. However, he's currently on vacation in Okinawa with some friends who went to the beach without him.
phrases.notes: souji: cleaning; sweeping; dusting; scrubbing

phrases.japanese: さっきお兄さんを呼んでくるって言って走ってたんだ
phrases.reading: さっき おにいさん を よんで くる って いって はしってた ん だ
phrases.lemmaField: さっき お兄さん を 呼ぶ くる って 言う 走る ん だ
phrases.romaji: sakki oniisan wo yonde kuru tte itte hashitteta n da
phrases.translation: A while ago [she] said: [I go and call my brother] and went off.
phrases.notes:
hashiru: to run
Difficult sentence, hints: tte itte is "to iu" in it's -te form. "xxx to iu" means "to say xxx". The -te form then links it to the next part of the sentence (hashitteta), which is from hashitte ita.

phrases.reading: まど から はなれてて
phrases.lemmaField: 窓 から 離れる
phrases.translation: Stay away from the window...!
phrases.notes:
mado: window
hanareru: to be separated, to go away

hanaretete: colloquial shortening of hanarete ite, ite being the -te form of "iru". So we have an enduring state here, hence the "stay away" in the translation.

phrases.reading: たとえば
phrases.lemmaField: 例えば
phrases.translation: tatoeba: for example

phrases.japanese: この傘よかったらあんた使ってよ
phrases.reading: この かさ よかったら あんた つかって よ
phrases.lemmaField: この 傘 よい あんた 使う よ
phrases.romaji: kono kasa yokattara anta tsukatte yo
phrases.translation: This umbrella, if [you] like, you can use it.
phrases.notes: tsukau: to use (a tool, method, etc.); to make use of; to put to use

phrases.japanese: お母さんお父さんと結婚できて幸せだったから
phrases.reading: おかあさん おとうさん と けっこん できて しあわせ だった から
phrases.lemmaField: お母さん お父さん と 結婚 できる 幸せ だ から
phrases.romaji: okaasan otousan to kekkon dekite shiawase datta kara
phrases.translation: As for mom, [she] was happy because she could marry dad.
phrases.grammarNote: Ignore the trailing "kara", the conversation continues a bit.
phrases.notes:
kekkon: marriage (this ranks surprisingly high on my frequency lists)
Reminder: The -te form can be used to express a reason, have a look at the reference.

phrases.japanese: 世界に２人しかいない感じしない
phrases.reading: せかい に ふたり しか いない かんじ しない
phrases.lemmaField: 世界 に ２人 しか いる 感じ する
phrases.romaji: sekai ni futari shika inai kanji shinai
phrases.translation: Doesn't [this] feel like there are only two people / the two of us in the world? (They are sitting together in an empty classroom).
phrases.notes:
kanji: feeling; sense; impression
The word "kanji" is not only a Chinese character, but it also has this completely different meaning. I often found this quite hard to translate.

phrases.japanese: もう少し大きい声で歌いなさい
phrases.reading: もうすこし おおきい こえ で うたい なさい
phrases.lemmaField: もう少し 大きい 声 で 歌う なさる
phrases.romaji: mousukoshi ookii koe de utai nasai
phrases.translation: Sing with a slightly louder / larger voice.
phrases.notes:
utau: to sing
Reminder: verb stem + nasai = firm, but polite order

phrases.reading: まさか
phrases.lemmaField: まさか
phrases.translation: No way! By no means [can this be true]!
phrases.notes:
"masaka" is not always easy to translate directly. It is very common though and usually means, that something is unbelievable and not likely to be true. 
The official dictionary definition is: by no means; never!; well, I never!; you don't say!; certainly (not)

phrases.japanese: うんトイレ掃除とか上手だよな
phrases.reading: うん といれ そうじ とか じょうず だ よ な
phrases.lemmaField: うん トイレ 掃除 とか 上手 だ よ な
phrases.romaji: un toire souji toka jouzu da yo na
phrases.translation: [And you, ramuchi, you are] good at cleaning toilets, right? -> the guy is trying to compliment one of the girls. Probably not the right words :D
phrases.notes: souji: cleaning; sweeping; dusting; scrubbing
phrases.source: Re Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (Eng + Jp)

phrases.japanese: まさか本当に食べてないのか
phrases.reading: まさか ほんとうに たべてない の か
phrases.lemmaField: まさか 本当に 食べる の か ほんとに
phrases.translation: No way, [you are] really not eating [this delicious food]?
phrases.notes:
"masaka" is not always easy to translate directly. It is very common though and usually means, that something is unbelievable and not likely to be true. 
The official dictionary definition is: by no means; never!; well, I never!; you don't say!; certainly (not)

phrases.japanese: そんなふうに考えてはいけないと思っていた
phrases.reading: そんな ふう に かんがえて は いけない と おもって いた
phrases.lemmaField: そんな ふう に 考える は いける と 思う いる
phrases.romaji: sonna fuu ni kangaete ha ikenai to omotte ita
phrases.translation: [I] thought [you] must not think that way
phrases.notes: fuu: method; manner; way; style

phrases.reading: つかって くれ おれ の からだ を
phrases.lemmaField: 使う くれる 俺 の 体 を 使い方
phrases.romaji: tsukatte kure ore no karada wo
phrases.translation: Do [me] the favor of using [it], my body [I mean].
phrases.notes: tsukau: to use (a tool, method, etc.); to make use of; to put to use

phrases.japanese: 殺す前にぜひ聞きたいことがある
phrases.reading: ころす まえ に ぜひ ききたい こと が ある
phrases.lemmaField: 殺す 前 に ぜひ 聞く こと が ある 是非 ぜひぜひ
phrases.romaji: korosu mae ni zehi kikitai koto ga aru
phrases.translation: Before [I] kill [you], [I] by all means want to know thing is there -> there's something I want to know by all means, before I kill you.
phrases.notes: zehi: by all means; certainly; definitely
phrases.source: Legend of the Galactic Heroes (JP Eng) (Media Added)

phrases.japanese: はいみんな登録してくれてありがとう
phrases.reading: はい みんな とうろく して くれて ありがとう
phrases.lemmaField: はい みんな 登録 する くれる ありがとう
phrases.romaji: hai minna touroku shite kurete arigatou
phrases.translation: Ok, thanks everyone for giving me the favor of subscribing!
phrases.notes: touroku: registration, subscription; this is a word you'll often hear in youtube videos ;)

phrases.japanese: 話は以上だ聞いてくれてありがとう
phrases.reading: はなし は いじょう だ きいて くれて ありがとう
phrases.lemmaField: 話 は 以上 だ 聞く くれる ありがとう
phrases.romaji: hanashi ha ijou da kiite kurete arigatou
phrases.translation: As for conversation, that's all. Thank you for giving me the favor of listening.
phrases.notes:
ijou: that's all; that is the end; the end
Again a word I often found hard to translate, probably because a different meaning of "ijou" is "beyond, more than", see one of the next cards.

phrases.japanese: いつもこんな感じなの
phrases.reading: いつも こんな かんじ な の
phrases.lemmaField: いつも こんな 感じ だ の
phrases.translation: Does [it] always feel like this? lit: Is [it] always this feeling?
phrases.notes:
kanji: feeling; sense; impression
The word "kanji" is not only a Chinese character, but it also has this completely different meaning. I often found this quite hard to translate.

phrases.japanese: 俺に言えることは以上だ
phrases.reading: おれ に いえる こと は いじょう だ
phrases.lemmaField: 俺 に 言える こと は 以上 だ いえる
phrases.romaji: ore ni ieru koto ha ijou da
phrases.translation: As for what-I-can-say thing, that's all -> This is all I can say.
phrases.notes:
ijou: that's all; that is the end; the end
Again a word I often found hard to translate, probably because a different meaning of "ijou" is "beyond, more than", see one of the next cards.

phrases.japanese: 待ってまさか本当に言いたいことがあるのか
phrases.reading: まって まさか ほんとうに いいたい こと が ある の か
phrases.lemmaField: 待つ まさか 本当に 言う こと が ある の か
phrases.romaji: matte masaka hontouni iitai koto ga aru no ka
phrases.translation: Wait, you gotta be kidding, is there really something [you] want to say?
phrases.notes:
"masaka" is not always easy to translate directly. It is very common though and usually means, that something is unbelievable and not likely to be true. 
The official dictionary definition is: by no means; never!; well, I never!; you don't say!; certainly (not)

Reminder: iu (to say) -> iitai (want to say)

phrases.japanese: ありがとう今日聞きたかったことは以上です
phrases.reading: ありがとう きょう ききたかった こと は いじょう です
phrases.lemmaField: ありがとう 今日 聞く こと は 以上 です
phrases.romaji: arigatou kyou kikitakatta koto ha ijou desu
phrases.translation: Thank you. As for [what I] wanted to ask today thing, that's all -> this is all I wanted to ask you today. Note that "koto" can in many cases not be translated to English directly, but you'll get used to this over time, trust me ;).
phrases.notes:
ijou: that's all; that is the end; the end
Again a word I often found hard to translate, probably because a different meaning of "ijou" is "beyond, more than", see one of the next cards.

Reminder: kiku -> kikitai -> kikitakatta (wanted to ask)

phrases.japanese: ちょっとそういう言い方は良くないよ
phrases.reading: ちょっと そういう いいかた は よくない よ
phrases.lemmaField: ちょっと そういう 言い方 は 良い よ
phrases.romaji: chotto souiu iikata ha yokunai yo
phrases.translation: Come on, that way-of-saying is not good -> don't put it that way.
phrases.notes: souiu: such; like that; that sort of​ (refers to something close to the listener, just as for sore / kore)

phrases.japanese: だからってこんなふうに勝っても全然うれしくないよ
phrases.reading: だ から って こんな ふう に かって も ぜんぜん うれしくない よ
phrases.lemmaField: だ から って こんな ふう に 勝つ も 全然 うれしい よ
phrases.romaji: da kara tte konna fuu ni katte mo zenzen ureshikunai yo
phrases.translation: ...but even if [I] win this way, it's totally not joyful/delightful -> I don't want to win like this [the speaker is about to win a fight, because the opponent gave up].
phrases.notes:
fuu: method; manner; way; style

The pattern -te mo can be used to express: even if / regardless / no matter what.

phrases.japanese: これ以上なにをする気だ
phrases.reading: これ いじょう なに を する き だ
phrases.lemmaField: これ 以上 なに を する 気 だ
phrases.romaji: kore ijou nani wo suru ki da
phrases.translation: Beyond this, what-do intention is it? This sort of means: What else do you intend to do beyond this? Do you want to cause even more trouble?
phrases.notes:
ijou: beyond, more than

ki: motivation, intention
I'd say the major meaning of "ki" is "spirit; mind; heart​". What I found very interesting is that all other meanings such as "motivation, intention" can somehow be mapped to "spirit, mind".

phrases.japanese: 読めない漢字があったら教えてやるぞん
phrases.reading: よめない かんじ が あったら おしえて やる ぞん
phrases.lemmaField: 読める 漢字 が ある 教える やる ぞ
phrases.romaji: yomenai kanji ga attara oshiete yaru zon
phrases.translation: If there's a cannot-read kanji, [I] teach [you].
phrases.notes:
kanji: Chinese character, which makes reading Japanese a nightmare (or fun, choose your favorite :D)

Note the -te yaru construction. Here, we do not have a physical action. Instead, this is used to express the listener's lower status. A more friendly way to express this would be to use -te ageru.

phrases.japanese: それを言うために待っていた
phrases.reading: それ を いう ために まって いた
phrases.lemmaField: それ を 言う ため 待つ いる
phrases.romaji: sore wo iu tameni matte ita
phrases.translation: [I] have been waiting for the purpose of telling [you] that.
phrases.notes:
tame ni: for; for the sake of; in order to
Here, tame is described by a clause (sore-wo-iu).
phrases.source: The Disastrous Life of Saiki K. (Eng + Jp)

phrases.japanese: こういうのは時間がかかる
phrases.reading: こういう の は じかん が かかる
phrases.lemmaField: こういう の は 時間 が かかる
phrases.romaji: kouiu no ha jikan ga kakaru
phrases.translation: [Things] like this take time.
phrases.notes: kouiu: such; this sort of; like this (refers to something close to the speaker, just as for sore / kore)

phrases.japanese: 自分のことも嫌いにならないで
phrases.reading: じぶん の こと も きらい に ならない で
phrases.lemmaField: 自分 の こと も 嫌い に なる で
phrases.romaji: jibun no koto mo kirai ni naranai de
phrases.translation: Don't start to hate yourself...
phrases.notes:
kirai: disliked; hated; disagreeable
Remark: "mo" is used for emphasis here, which is a frequent use case. Have a look at the references.

phrases.japanese: もっと走らせるべきだったか
phrases.reading: もっと はしらせる べき だった か
phrases.lemmaField: もっと 走る べし だ か
phrases.translation: Should [I] have made them running more? -> Looks like the guy is a trainer, this anime is about running.
phrases.notes:
hashiru: to run
Reminder 1: hashiraseru is causative: to make or to let someone do something - running in this case.
Reminder 2: beki is used to express "should"

phrases.japanese: 結局お前はそういう奴なんだ
phrases.reading: けっきょく おまえ は そういう やつ なんだ
phrases.lemmaField: 結局 お前 は そういう 奴 なんだ
phrases.romaji: kekkyoku omae ha souiu yatsu nanda
phrases.translation: So in the end, you are that sort of person -> looks like the speaker just realized the true nature of the listener.
phrases.notes: souiu: such; like that; that sort of​ (refers to something close to the listener, just as for sore / kore)

phrases.japanese: 大丈夫お腹お腹痛いの
phrases.reading: だいじょうぶ おなか おなか いたい の
phrases.lemmaField: 大丈夫 お腹 お腹 痛い の
phrases.translation: [Are you] Ok? Stomach? Does [your] stomach hurt?
phrases.notes: onaka: stomach, belly

phrases.japanese: ダメだダメだこれ以上考えるな
phrases.reading: だめ だ だめ だ これ いじょう かんがえる な
phrases.lemmaField: ダメ だ ダメ だ これ 以上 考える な
phrases.romaji: dame da dame da kore ijou kangaeru na
phrases.translation: It's bad, it's bad, do not think about [it] beyond this point [i.e. do not think any further].

phrases.japanese: しまった俺のノドがあがああ
phrases.reading: しまった おれ の のど が あ が ああ
phrases.lemmaField: しまる 俺 の ノド が あ が ああ
phrases.romaji: shimatta ore no nodo ga a ga aa
phrases.translation: Damn it, my throat, grwafawr -> Sounds like the poor guy gets choked by something...
phrases.notes: nodo: throat
phrases.source: JoJos Bizarre Adventure 黄金の風 (26-39)

phrases.reading: どうしたん だ それ は
phrases.lemmaField: どうしたん だ それ は よくある
phrases.translation: What happened? As for that [you in this small jar, I mean]
phrases.notes:
doushitan: what happened? What's the matter?
This actually is: dou shita no with the last "no" just as "n". Literally, it means: what/how was [it] (from dou shita), the additional "no" is the explanatory one, which in a question means that an explanation is desired.

Caution, this is rather informal.

phrases.reading: いっしゅうかん くらい まえ か な
phrases.lemmaField: １週間 くらい 前 か な
phrases.translation: [It was] about one week ago, wasn't it?
phrases.notes:
kurai: approximately, about, around (sometimes also spelled "gurai", used to make expressions or numbers more vague)
isshuukan: one week

Just learn isshuukan as "one week" for now. This is actually build from:
ichi - one
shuu - week
kan - period of time
I found counting boring and a nighmare for several reasons, every 5 year old Japanese kid can probably do it better than me. This will be put into a separate deck.
phrases.source: からかい上手の高木さん

phrases.japanese: どうして英語で歌ってくれないんですか
phrases.reading: どうして えいご で うたって くれない ん です か
phrases.lemmaField: どうして 英語 で 歌う くれる ん だ か んです
phrases.romaji: doushite eigo de utatte kurenai n desu ka
phrases.translation: Why don't [you] sing in English [for me]?
phrases.notes: utau: to sing

phrases.japanese: 試合が終わったなんてまだ信じられないや
phrases.reading: しあい が おわった なんて まだ しんじられない や
phrases.lemmaField: 試合 が 終わる なんて まだ 信じる や
phrases.romaji: shiai ga owatta nante mada shinjirarenai ya
phrases.translation: That the match is over, [I] still can't believe (maybe it was a fight against a very tough opponent)
